final_response:
Here is a comprehensive plan for a National Park Nature and Wellness Workshop Series for Teachers in North Carolina, based on your requirements for hiking, guided nature walks, wellness programs, safety, amenities, and relevant summer events (July 15–August 15, 2025):

---

## Recommended Parks in North Carolina

### 1. Great Smoky Mountains National Park (GRSM)
- **Activities:** Extensive hiking, guided nature walks, ranger-led wellness and educational programs.
- **Campgrounds:** Multiple options including Cades Cove (group sites available), Balsam Mountain, Abrams Creek, and Big Creek. All have potable water, flush toilets, and are reservable.
- **Visitor Centers:** Sugarlands and Oconaluftee Visitor Centers offer information, restrooms, and educational exhibits.
- **Upcoming Events:** 
  - *Hiking 101* (tips and basics for hiking)
  - *Kuwohi Guided Hike* (ranger-led hike to the highest peak)
  - *Vital Signs of the Smokies* (wellness and ecosystem health)
  - *Bear With Us!* and *Bear Aware in Cades Cove* (wildlife safety)
  - *Stream Splashers* (nature connection and wellness)
  - *Drop into History* (cultural wellness)
- **Alerts:** Some road closures (Park Headquarters Road, Old NC 284, Balsam Mountain Road), but main campgrounds and visitor centers remain accessible. Check for updates before travel.
- **Safety:** Bear safety and food storage regulations in place. Ranger programs cover wildlife safety.
- **Links:** [Park Info](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/index.htm), [Campground Reservations](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232488)

---

### 2. Blue Ridge Parkway (BLRI)
- **Activities:** Hiking, scenic walks, ranger-guided programs, wellness through music and nature.
- **Visitor Centers:** 
  - Blue Ridge Parkway Visitor Center (Asheville, NC)
  - Blue Ridge Music Center (Galax, VA/NC border)
- **Upcoming Events:**
  - *Midday Mountain Music* (daily, Blue Ridge Music Center)
  - *Milepost Music* (Doughton Park, NC, July 13 & 27, August 10 & 24)
  - *Brinegar Cabin Open House* (Doughton Park, July 13, August 10)
  - *Guided Tours at Moses H. Cone Manor House* (Milepost 294, near Boone/Blowing Rock)
- **Alerts:** Some road closures for maintenance and Helene recovery projects; check [road status](https://www.nps.gov/blri/planyourvisit/road-construction-projects.htm).
- **Wellness Focus:** Music, history, and nature walks support teacher wellness.
- **Links:** [Park Info](https://www.nps.gov/blri/index.htm)

---

### 3. Cape Hatteras National Seashore (CAHA)
- **Activities:** Beach hiking, ranger-led nature walks, wellness and environmental programs.
- **Campgrounds:** Multiple front-country and group campgrounds available.
- **Visitor Centers:** Hatteras Island Visitor Center, Bodie Island Visitor Center.
- **Upcoming Events:**
  - *Life on a Barrier Island* (daily, Hatteras/Bodie/Ocracoke)
  - *Totally Turtles!* (sea turtle wellness and conservation)
  - *Dark Skies Over Hatteras* (wellness through stargazing)
  - *Crabbing with a Ranger*, *Bird Walk*, *Kayak with a Ranger* (nature connection)
- **Safety:** Standard beach and wildlife safety protocols.
- **Links:** [Park Info](https://www.nps.gov/caha/index.htm)

---

## Summary Table

| Park                        | Hiking & Nature Walks | Wellness Programs/Events | Campgrounds | Visitor Centers | Safety/Alerts |
|-----------------------------|----------------------|-------------------------|-------------|----------------|---------------|
| Great Smoky Mountains NP    | Yes                  | Yes (guided hikes, wellness, nature) | Yes (multiple, group sites) | Yes (Sugarlands, Oconaluftee) | Some road closures, bear safety |
| Blue Ridge Parkway          | Yes                  | Yes (music, history, guided walks) | Limited (check for group options) | Yes (Asheville, Music Center) | Road closures in some areas |
| Cape Hatteras NS            | Yes                  | Yes (beach walks, turtles, stargazing) | Yes (front-country, group) | Yes (multiple) | Standard beach safety |

---

## Recommendations for Workshop Planning

- **Best for Overnight, Group, and Wellness Focus:** Great Smoky Mountains National Park (Cades Cove or B

Here is a comprehensive plan for a National Park Nature and Wellness Workshop Series for Teachers in North Carolina, based on your requirements for hiking, guided nature walks, wellness programs, safety, amenities, and relevant summer events (July 15–August 15, 2025):

---

## Recommended Parks in North Carolina

### 1. Great Smoky Mountains National Park (GRSM)
- **Activities:** Extensive hiking, guided nature walks, ranger-led wellness and educational programs.
- **Campgrounds:** Multiple options including Cades Cove (group sites available), Balsam Mountain, Abrams Creek, and Big Creek. All have potable water, flush toilets, and are reservable.
- **Visitor Centers:** Sugarlands and Oconaluftee Visitor Centers offer information, restrooms, and educational exhibits.
- **Upcoming Events:** 
  - *Hiking 101* (tips and basics for hiking)
  - *Kuwohi Guided Hike* (ranger-led hike to the highest peak)
  - *Vital Signs of the Smokies* (wellness and ecosystem health)
  - *Bear With Us!* and *Bear Aware in Cades Cove* (wildlife safety)
  - *Stream Splashers* (nature connection and wellness)
  - *Drop into History* (cultural wellness)
- **Alerts:** Some road closures (Park Headquarters Road, Old NC 284, Balsam Mountain Road), but main campgrounds and visitor centers remain accessible. Check for updates before travel.
- **Safety:** Bear safety and food storage regulations in place. Ranger programs cover wildlife safety.
- **Links:** [Park Info](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/index.htm), [Campground Reservations](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232488)

---

### 2. Blue Ridge Parkway (BLRI)
- **Activities:** Hiking, scenic walks, ranger-guided programs, wellness through music and nature.
- **Visitor Centers:** 
  - Blue Ridge Parkway Visitor Center (Asheville, NC)
  - Blue Ridge Music Center (Galax, VA/NC border)
- **Upcoming Events:**
  - *Midday Mountain Music* (daily, Blue Ridge Music Center)
  - *Milepost Music* (Doughton Park, NC, July 13 & 27, August 10 & 24)
  - *Brinegar Cabin Open House* (Doughton Park, July 13, August 10)
  - *Guided Tours at Moses H. Cone Manor House* (Milepost 294, near Boone/Blowing Rock)
- **Alerts:** Some road closures for maintenance and Helene recovery projects; check [road status](https://www.nps.gov/blri/planyourvisit/road-construction-projects.htm).
- **Wellness Focus:** Music, history, and nature walks support teacher wellness.
- **Links:** [Park Info](https://www.nps.gov/blri/index.htm)

---

### 3. Cape Hatteras National Seashore (CAHA)
- **Activities:** Beach hiking, ranger-led nature walks, wellness and environmental programs.
- **Campgrounds:** Multiple front-country and group campgrounds available.
- **Visitor Centers:** Hatteras Island Visitor Center, Bodie Island Visitor Center.
- **Upcoming Events:**
  - *Life on a Barrier Island* (daily, Hatteras/Bodie/Ocracoke)
  - *Totally Turtles!* (sea turtle wellness and conservation)
  - *Dark Skies Over Hatteras* (wellness through stargazing)
  - *Crabbing with a Ranger*, *Bird Walk*, *Kayak with a Ranger* (nature connection)
- **Safety:** Standard beach and wildlife safety protocols.
- **Links:** [Park Info](https://www.nps.gov/caha/index.htm)

---

## Summary Table

| Park                        | Hiking & Nature Walks | Wellness Programs/Events | Campgrounds | Visitor Centers | Safety/Alerts |
|-----------------------------|----------------------|-------------------------|-------------|----------------|---------------|
| Great Smoky Mountains NP    | Yes                  | Yes (guided hikes, wellness, nature) | Yes (multiple, group sites) | Yes (Sugarlands, Oconaluftee) | Some road closures, bear safety |
| Blue Ridge Parkway          | Yes                  | Yes (music, history, guided walks) | Limited (check for group options) | Yes (Asheville, Music Center) | Road closures in some areas |
| Cape Hatteras NS            | Yes                  | Yes (beach walks, turtles, stargazing) | Yes (front-country, group) | Yes (multiple) | Standard beach safety |

final_response:
Here is a comprehensive plan and resource guide for your week-long Art and Nature Journaling Retreat in Great Smoky Mountains National Park, July 10–17, 2025:

—
**1. Park Selection & Overview**
- **Best Park:** Great Smoky Mountains National Park (GRSM) is ideal for your retreat, renowned for its biodiversity, scenic beauty, and cultural history.
- **Location:** Straddles the border of North Carolina and Tennessee.
- **Main Entrances:** Gatlinburg, TN; Townsend, TN; Cherokee, NC.
- **Official Website:** [nps.gov/grsm](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/index.htm)
- **Contact:** (865) 436-1200 | GRSM_Smokies_Information@nps.gov

—
**2. Park Details**
- **Description:** Ancient mountains, lush forests, wildflowers, and historic structures. Offers activities in arts, culture, hiking, wildlife watching, and more.
- **Weather:** Elevations range from 875–6,643 ft. Temperatures can vary 10–20°F from base to summit. Be prepared for sudden weather changes.
- **Operating Hours:** Primary roads open 24/7, year-round (weather permitting).

—
**3. Current Alerts & Closures (as of July 2025)**
- **Park Headquarters Road Closed:** Through September 2025. Use Sugarlands Visitor Center for access to certain trails.
- **Old NC 284 Closed:** No access to Cataloochee Valley due to road damage.
- **Cades Cove Loop Road:** Closed to motor vehicles every Wednesday (June 18–Sept 24) for pedestrian/cyclist enjoyment.
- **Straight Fork & Balsam Mountain Road:** Some sections closed; Balsam Mountain Campground accessible.
- **Parking Tag Required:** All vehicles parked more than 15 minutes need a tag (Daily $5, Weekly $15, Annual $40). [Details](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/fees.htm)

—
**4. Visitor Centers (for Orientation Sessions)**
- **Sugarlands Visitor Center** (Gatlinburg, TN): Natural history exhibits, ranger-led programs, bookstore, restrooms.
  - 1420 Fighting Creek Gap Road, Gatlinburg, TN 37738
  - Hours: 9am–5pm daily
  - [Visitor Center Info](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/visitorcenters.htm)
- **Oconaluftee Visitor Center** (Cherokee, NC): Cultural history exhibits, ranger-led programs, Mountain Farm Museum.
  - 1194 Newfound Gap Road, Cherokee, NC 28719
  - Hours: 9am–5pm daily
- **Cades Cove Visitor Center** (Townsend, TN): Historic structures, seasonal ranger activities.
  - Cable Mill Road, Townsend, TN 37882
  - Hours: 9am–5pm daily
- **Kuwohi Visitor Center** (Clingmans Dome): Scenic views, bookstore, restrooms.
  - Clingmans Dome Road, Cherokee, NC 28719
  - Hours: 9:30am–6pm daily (seasonal)

—
**5. Campgrounds (for Group Lodging)**
- **Elkmont Campground** (Closest to Sugarlands Visitor Center)
  - 434 Elkmont Road, Gatlinburg, TN 37738
  - 211 sites, 4 group sites, $30/night (group: $26–$53/night)
  - Open March 14–Nov 30, 2025. Reservations required.
  - [Reserve Elkmont](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232487)
- **Elkmont Group Campground**
  - 4 group tent-only sites (15–30 people per site)
  - [Reserve Group Sites](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232436)
- **Cades Cove Campground & Group Campground**
  - 161 sites, 4 group sites, $30/night (group: $35–$65/night)
  - [Reserve Cades Cove](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232488) | [Group](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232440)
- **Other Options:** Cosby, Deep Creek, Balsam Mountain, Abrams Creek, Cataloochee (see above for details).

—
**6. Relevant Events (July 10–17, 2025)**
- No ranger-led art walks, journaling workshops, or similar events are currently scheduled for this week. However, visitor centers often offer seasonal ranger-led programs—check closer to your retreat for updates.

—
**

Here is a comprehensive plan and resource guide for your week-long Art and Nature Journaling Retreat in Great Smoky Mountains National Park, July 10–17, 2025:

—
**1. Park Selection & Overview**
- **Best Park:** Great Smoky Mountains National Park (GRSM) is ideal for your retreat, renowned for its biodiversity, scenic beauty, and cultural history.
- **Location:** Straddles the border of North Carolina and Tennessee.
- **Main Entrances:** Gatlinburg, TN; Townsend, TN; Cherokee, NC.
- **Official Website:** [nps.gov/grsm](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/index.htm)
- **Contact:** (865) 436-1200 | GRSM_Smokies_Information@nps.gov

—
**2. Park Details**
- **Description:** Ancient mountains, lush forests, wildflowers, and historic structures. Offers activities in arts, culture, hiking, wildlife watching, and more.
- **Weather:** Elevations range from 875–6,643 ft. Temperatures can vary 10–20°F from base to summit. Be prepared for sudden weather changes.
- **Operating Hours:** Primary roads open 24/7, year-round (weather permitting).

—
**3. Current Alerts & Closures (as of July 2025)**
- **Park Headquarters Road Closed:** Through September 2025. Use Sugarlands Visitor Center for access to certain trails.
- **Old NC 284 Closed:** No access to Cataloochee Valley due to road damage.
- **Cades Cove Loop Road:** Closed to motor vehicles every Wednesday (June 18–Sept 24) for pedestrian/cyclist enjoyment.
- **Straight Fork & Balsam Mountain Road:** Some sections closed; Balsam Mountain Campground accessible.
- **Parking Tag Required:** All vehicles parked more than 15 minutes need a tag (Daily $5, Weekly $15, Annual $40). [Details](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/fees.htm)

—
**4. Visitor Centers (for Orientation Sessions)**
- **Sugarlands Visitor Center** (Gatlinburg, TN): Natural history exhibits, ranger-led programs, bookstore, restrooms.
  - 1420 Fighting Creek Gap Road, Gatlinburg, TN 37738
  - Hours: 9am–5pm daily
  - [Visitor Center Info](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/visitorcenters.htm)
- **Oconaluftee Visitor Center** (Cherokee, NC): Cultural history exhibits, ranger-led programs, Mountain Farm Museum.
  - 1194 Newfound Gap Road, Cherokee, NC 28719
  - Hours: 9am–5pm daily
- **Cades Cove Visitor Center** (Townsend, TN): Historic structures, seasonal ranger activities.
  - Cable Mill Road, Townsend, TN 37882
  - Hours: 9am–5pm daily
- **Kuwohi Visitor Center** (Clingmans Dome): Scenic views, bookstore, restrooms.
  - Clingmans Dome Road, Cherokee, NC 28719
  - Hours: 9:30am–6pm daily (seasonal)

—
**5. Campgrounds (for Group Lodging)**
- **Elkmont Campground** (Closest to Sugarlands Visitor Center)
  - 434 Elkmont Road, Gatlinburg, TN 37738
  - 211 sites, 4 group sites, $30/night (group: $26–$53/night)
  - Open March 14–Nov 30, 2025. Reservations required.
  - [Reserve Elkmont](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232487)
- **Elkmont Group Campground**
  - 4 group tent-only sites (15–30 people per site)
  - [Reserve Group Sites](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232436)
- **Cades Cove Campground & Group Campground**
  - 161 sites, 4 group sites, $30/night (group: $35–$65/night)
  - [Reserve Cades Cove](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232488) | [Group](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232440)
- **Other Options:** Cosby, Deep Creek, Balsam Mountain, Abrams Creek, Cataloochee (see above for details).

—
**6. Relevant Events (July 10–17, 2025)**
- No ranger-led art walks, journaling workshops, or similar events are currently scheduled for this week. However, visitor centers often offer seasonal ranger-led programs—check closer to your retreat for updates.

—
**

final_response:
Here is a comprehensive plan for a week-long National Park Art Retreat at Bandelier National Monument, New Mexico, including park selection, logistics, and art-related opportunities:

---
## Park Selection: Bandelier National Monument

**Why Bandelier?**
- Over 33,000 acres of stunning canyons, mesas, petroglyphs, and cliff dwellings.
- Renowned for its scenic views and rich cultural history.
- Offers arts and culture activities, craft demonstrations, and regular cultural events.
- Multiple hiking trails, wildlife, and unique landscapes for artistic inspiration.

**Location:**  
15 Entrance Road, Los Alamos, NM 87544  
[Official Park Website](https://www.nps.gov/band/index.htm)

---

## Logistics

### 1. Park Details & Orientation

- **Visitor Center:**  
  Bandelier National Monument Visitor Center (Frijoles Canyon)  
  Hours: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM daily  
  Phone: (505) 672-3861 ext. 1800  
  Email: band_visitor_center@nps.gov  
  [Visitor Center Info & Directions](http://www.nps.gov/band/planyourvisit/directions.htm)

- **Operating Hours:**  
  Park open sunrise to sunset.

- **Entrance Fees:**  
  - Private Vehicle: $25  
  - Motorcycle: $20  
  - Per Person (walk/bike): $15  
  - Annual Park Pass: $45

- **Weather in July:**  
  Warm, dry days with possible afternoon thunderstorms. Prepare for sun and rain.

### 2. Campgrounds (Accommodation)

- **Juniper Family Campground**  
  - 52 sites (mostly first-come, first-served; some group sites reservable)  
  - Fee: $20/night per site (up to 2 vehicles)  
  - Amenities: Flush toilets, potable water, amphitheater, camp store, firewood for sale, ADA accessible sites  
  - [Campground Info](https://www.nps.gov/band/planyourvisit/juniper-family-campground.htm)  
  - [Reservations for group sites](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/233395)

- **Ponderosa Group Campground**  
  - 2 large group sites (reservation required)  
  - Fee: $50/night per group site  
  - Tent camping only, pit toilets, seasonal water  
  - [Campground Info](https://www.nps.gov/band/planyourvisit/ponderosa-group-campground.htm)  
  - [Reservations](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/233394)

**Note:**  
- Ponderosa Campground is experiencing a temporary water outage—bring all needed water.
- Cell service is limited; plan accordingly for communication and ride arrangements.

### 3. Current Alerts (as of June 2025)

- Alcove House is temporarily closed due to ladder deterioration.
- Water outage at Ponderosa Campground—bring your own water.
- Limited cell service; Uber/Lyft may not be available for return trips.
- GPS may misroute visitors—follow official directions.

---

## Art-Related Activities & Events (July 10–17, 2025)

### Scheduled Events

- **Cultural Demonstration by Sheila Martinez**
  - Dates: July 11 & July 13, 2025
  - Location: Back patio of the Bandelier Visitor Center
  - Description: Free, open to the public. Experience traditional arts and crafts demonstrations by a local artist. Supported by Friends of Bandelier.
  - Great opportunity for artists to observe, learn, and interact with local culture.

- **Falls Trail Geology Hike**
  - Date: July 13, 2025
  - Description: Guided hike with geologists along the scenic Falls Trail, focusing on the area's geology. Inspiring for landscape and nature artists.

### Ongoing Opportunities

- **Arts and Culture Activities:**  
  Regular craft and cultural demonstrations, museum exhibits, and opportunities to sketch/paint the ruins, petroglyphs, and landscapes.

- **Scenic Inspiration:**  
  - Frijoles Canyon, Tyuonyi ruins, cliff dwellings, Valles Caldera views, and the Rio Grande.
  - Wildlife and wildflowers in summer.

---

## Summary Plan

1. **Base your retreat at Bandelier National Monument for its blend of natural beauty and cultural richness.**
2. **Reserve group or individual campsites at Juniper Family or Ponderosa Campgrounds (bring water if using Ponderosa).**
3. **Begin your visit at the Bandelier Visitor Center for orientation and information.**
4. **Attend the art/cultural demonstrations and geology hike for group inspiration and learning.**

Here is a comprehensive plan for a week-long National Park Art Retreat at Bandelier National Monument, New Mexico, including park selection, logistics, and art-related opportunities:

---
## Park Selection: Bandelier National Monument

**Why Bandelier?**
- Over 33,000 acres of stunning canyons, mesas, petroglyphs, and cliff dwellings.
- Renowned for its scenic views and rich cultural history.
- Offers arts and culture activities, craft demonstrations, and regular cultural events.
- Multiple hiking trails, wildlife, and unique landscapes for artistic inspiration.

**Location:**  
15 Entrance Road, Los Alamos, NM 87544  
[Official Park Website](https://www.nps.gov/band/index.htm)

---

## Logistics

### 1. Park Details & Orientation

- **Visitor Center:**  
  Bandelier National Monument Visitor Center (Frijoles Canyon)  
  Hours: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM daily  
  Phone: (505) 672-3861 ext. 1800  
  Email: band_visitor_center@nps.gov  
  [Visitor Center Info & Directions](http://www.nps.gov/band/planyourvisit/directions.htm)

- **Operating Hours:**  
  Park open sunrise to sunset.

- **Entrance Fees:**  
  - Private Vehicle: $25  
  - Motorcycle: $20  
  - Per Person (walk/bike): $15  
  - Annual Park Pass: $45

- **Weather in July:**  
  Warm, dry days with possible afternoon thunderstorms. Prepare for sun and rain.

### 2. Campgrounds (Accommodation)

- **Juniper Family Campground**  
  - 52 sites (mostly first-come, first-served; some group sites reservable)  
  - Fee: $20/night per site (up to 2 vehicles)  
  - Amenities: Flush toilets, potable water, amphitheater, camp store, firewood for sale, ADA accessible sites  
  - [Campground Info](https://www.nps.gov/band/planyourvisit/juniper-family-campground.htm)  
  - [Reservations for group sites](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/233395)

- **Ponderosa Group Campground**  
  - 2 large group sites (reservation required)  
  - Fee: $50/night per group site  
  - Tent camping only, pit toilets, seasonal water  
  - [Campground Info](https://www.nps.gov/band/planyourvisit/ponderosa-group-campground.htm)  
  - [Reservations](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/233394)

**Note:**  
- Ponderosa Campground is experiencing a temporary water outage—bring all needed water.
- Cell service is limited; plan accordingly for communication and ride arrangements.

### 3. Current Alerts (as of June 2025)

- Alcove House is temporarily closed due to ladder deterioration.
- Water outage at Ponderosa Campground—bring your own water.
- Limited cell service; Uber/Lyft may not be available for return trips.
- GPS may misroute visitors—follow official directions.

---

## Art-Related Activities & Events (July 10–17, 2025)

### Scheduled Events

- **Cultural Demonstration by Sheila Martinez**
  - Dates: July 11 & July 13, 2025
  - Location: Back patio of the Bandelier Visitor Center
  - Description: Free, open to the public. Experience traditional arts and crafts demonstrations by a local artist. Supported by Friends of Bandelier.
  - Great opportunity for artists to observe, learn, and interact with local culture.

- **Falls Trail Geology Hike**
  - Date: July 13, 2025
  - Description: Guided hike with geologists along the scenic Falls Trail, focusing on the area's geology. Inspiring for landscape and nature artists.

### Ongoing Opportunities

- **Arts and Culture Activities:**  
  Regular craft and cultural demonstrations, museum exhibits, and opportunities to sketch/paint the ruins, petroglyphs, and landscapes.

- **Scenic Inspiration:**  
  - Frijoles Canyon, Tyuonyi ruins, cliff dwellings, Valles Caldera views, and the Rio Grande.
  - Wildlife and wildflowers in summer.

---

## Summary Plan

1. **Base your retreat at Bandelier National Monument for its blend of natural beauty and cultural richness.**
2. **Reserve group or individual campsites at Juniper Family or Ponderosa Campgrounds (bring water if using Ponderosa).**
3. **Begin your visit at the Bandelier Visitor Center for orientation and information.**
4. **Attend the art/cultural demonstrations and geology hike for group inspiration and learning.**

final_response:
Here is a comprehensive plan for your National Park Outdoor Skills and Survival Workshop Weekend in North Carolina, focused on the Blue Ridge Parkway, which offers excellent hiking and camping opportunities:

---

### 1. Park Selection: Blue Ridge Parkway
- The Blue Ridge Parkway is a premier destination in North Carolina for hiking and camping, with scenic vistas, diverse trails, and multiple campgrounds.
- Official Park Info: [Blue Ridge Parkway NPS](https://www.nps.gov/blri/index.htm)

---

### 2. Alerts & Hazards (as of June 2025)
- **Parkway Closures:** Some areas are closed due to ongoing road maintenance and Hurricane Helene recovery. Check the latest updates before your trip: [Road Construction Projects](https://www.nps.gov/blri/planyourvisit/road-construction-projects.htm)
- **Possible Hazards:** Open areas may have limited services and hazards such as landslides, tree debris, and washed-out trails/bridges. Use caution when hiking: [Road Closures & Hazards](https://www.nps.gov/blri/planyourvisit/roadclosures.htm)

---

### 3. Campgrounds (NC Section)
The following campgrounds are open and suitable for group workshops:

#### Doughton Park Campground
- **Location:** Laurel Springs, NC (Milepost 239.2)
- **Open:** June 13 – October 27, 2025
- **Sites:** 108 total (31 reservable, 77 first-come, first-served)
- **Group Sites:** Available (max 20 people)
- **Amenities:** Flush toilets, potable water, amphitheater, food storage lockers, camp store, no showers.
- **Accessibility:** 2 accessible sites.
- **Reservations:** [Recreation.gov - Doughton Park](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/233369)
- **More Info:** [NPS Doughton Park](https://www.nps.gov/blri/planyourvisit/doughton-park-cg.htm)
- **Contact:** (336) 372-8877

#### Mount Pisgah Campground
- **Location:** Near Asheville, NC (Milepost 408.8)
- **Open:** May 23 – October 27, 2025
- **Sites:** 125 total (53 reservable, 72 first-come, first-served)
- **Amenities:** Flush toilets, potable water, hot showers (seasonal), amphitheater, food storage lockers, camp store.
- **Accessibility:** 3 accessible sites.
- **Reservations:** [Recreation.gov - Mount Pisgah](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/234182)
- **More Info:** [NPS Mount Pisgah](https://www.nps.gov//blri/planyourvisit/mt-pisgah-cg.htm)
- **Contact:** (828) 648-2644

---

### 4. Visitor Centers (NC Section)
- **Blue Ridge Parkway Visitor Center (Asheville, MP 384):**
  - Open daily, 9:00 AM – 4:30 PM
  - Address: 195 Hemphill Knob Rd, Asheville, NC 28803
  - Phone: 828-298-5330 x304
  - [Visitor Center Info](http://www.nps.gov/blri/planyourvisit/blue-ridge-parkway-visitor-center.htm)

- **Doughton Park Visitor Center (MP 238):**
  - Open Wed–Sun, 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM
  - Address: 49800 Blue Ridge Parkway, Laurel Springs, NC 28644
  - Phone: (828) 348-3400
  - [Doughton Park Info](https://www.nps.gov/blri/planyourvisit/doughton-park.htm)

---

### 5. Ranger-led Events & Survival Workshops (June 28–29, 2025)
- No ranger-led survival workshops or outdoor skills events are currently scheduled for these dates on the Blue Ridge Parkway.
- **Recommendation:** Contact the visitor center or park rangers to inquire about scheduling a custom ranger-led program or to request a group educational session on outdoor skills and survival.

---

### 6. Additional Planning Notes
- **Weather:** Be prepared for rapidly changing mountain weather, especially afternoon thunderstorms.
- **Safety:** Due to recent hurricane impacts, check for the latest trail and road conditions before your trip.
- **Permits:** Standard camping fees apply; group sites are available at Doughton Park.
- **Contact:** For group reservations or special programs, reach out to the park’s visitor center or campground contacts above.

---

Would you like a sample itinerary, or help contacting the park for a custom ranger-led program?

Here is a comprehensive plan for your National Park Outdoor Skills and Survival Workshop Weekend in North Carolina, focused on the Blue Ridge Parkway, which offers excellent hiking and camping opportunities:

---

### 1. Park Selection: Blue Ridge Parkway
- The Blue Ridge Parkway is a premier destination in North Carolina for hiking and camping, with scenic vistas, diverse trails, and multiple campgrounds.
- Official Park Info: [Blue Ridge Parkway NPS](https://www.nps.gov/blri/index.htm)

---

### 2. Alerts & Hazards (as of June 2025)
- **Parkway Closures:** Some areas are closed due to ongoing road maintenance and Hurricane Helene recovery. Check the latest updates before your trip: [Road Construction Projects](https://www.nps.gov/blri/planyourvisit/road-construction-projects.htm)
- **Possible Hazards:** Open areas may have limited services and hazards such as landslides, tree debris, and washed-out trails/bridges. Use caution when hiking: [Road Closures & Hazards](https://www.nps.gov/blri/planyourvisit/roadclosures.htm)

---

### 3. Campgrounds (NC Section)
The following campgrounds are open and suitable for group workshops:

#### Doughton Park Campground
- **Location:** Laurel Springs, NC (Milepost 239.2)
- **Open:** June 13 – October 27, 2025
- **Sites:** 108 total (31 reservable, 77 first-come, first-served)
- **Group Sites:** Available (max 20 people)
- **Amenities:** Flush toilets, potable water, amphitheater, food storage lockers, camp store, no showers.
- **Accessibility:** 2 accessible sites.
- **Reservations:** [Recreation.gov - Doughton Park](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/233369)
- **More Info:** [NPS Doughton Park](https://www.nps.gov/blri/planyourvisit/doughton-park-cg.htm)
- **Contact:** (336) 372-8877

#### Mount Pisgah Campground
- **Location:** Near Asheville, NC (Milepost 408.8)
- **Open:** May 23 – October 27, 2025
- **Sites:** 125 total (53 reservable, 72 first-come, first-served)
- **Amenities:** Flush toilets, potable water, hot showers (seasonal), amphitheater, food storage lockers, camp store.
- **Accessibility:** 3 accessible sites.
- **Reservations:** [Recreation.gov - Mount Pisgah](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/234182)
- **More Info:** [NPS Mount Pisgah](https://www.nps.gov//blri/planyourvisit/mt-pisgah-cg.htm)
- **Contact:** (828) 648-2644

---

### 4. Visitor Centers (NC Section)
- **Blue Ridge Parkway Visitor Center (Asheville, MP 384):**
  - Open daily, 9:00 AM – 4:30 PM
  - Address: 195 Hemphill Knob Rd, Asheville, NC 28803
  - Phone: 828-298-5330 x304
  - [Visitor Center Info](http://www.nps.gov/blri/planyourvisit/blue-ridge-parkway-visitor-center.htm)

- **Doughton Park Visitor Center (MP 238):**
  - Open Wed–Sun, 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM
  - Address: 49800 Blue Ridge Parkway, Laurel Springs, NC 28644
  - Phone: (828) 348-3400
  - [Doughton Park Info](https://www.nps.gov/blri/planyourvisit/doughton-park.htm)

---

### 5. Ranger-led Events & Survival Workshops (June 28–29, 2025)
- No ranger-led survival workshops or outdoor skills events are currently scheduled for these dates on the Blue Ridge Parkway.
- **Recommendation:** Contact the visitor center or park rangers to inquire about scheduling a custom ranger-led program or to request a group educational session on outdoor skills and survival.

---

### 6. Additional Planning Notes
- **Weather:** Be prepared for rapidly changing mountain weather, especially afternoon thunderstorms.
- **Safety:** Due to recent hurricane impacts, check for the latest trail and road conditions before your trip.
- **Permits:** Standard camping fees apply; group sites are available at Doughton Park.
- **Contact:** For group reservations or special programs, reach out to the park’s visitor center or campground contacts above.

---

final_response:
Here’s a detailed plan for an accessible Astronomy and Night Hike Event in New Jersey national parks for July 2025, focusing on parks that offer both hiking and stargazing:

---
## 1. Recommended Parks in New Jersey

### Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area (DEWA)
- **Activities:** Hiking, stargazing, camping, paddling, wildlife watching.
- **Accessibility:** Bushkill Meeting Center (visitor center) and several campgrounds have accessible facilities.
- **Website:** [DEWA NPS](https://www.nps.gov/dewa/index.htm)

### Great Egg Harbor River (GREG)
- **Activities:** Hiking, stargazing, camping, paddling, birdwatching.
- **Note:** Local jurisdictions administer lands; check with Atlantic County Parks for accessibility details.
- **Website:** [Great Egg Harbor NPS](https://www.nps.gov/greg/index.htm)

### Appalachian National Scenic Trail (APPA) – NJ Section
- **Activities:** Hiking, stargazing, camping.
- **Note:** Some trail closures may persist due to storm damage; check for updates.
- **Website:** [Appalachian Trail NJ](https://www.nps.gov/appa/index.htm)

---
## 2. Current Alerts & Closures (July 2025)

### Delaware Water Gap
- **Dingmans Falls Trail, Visitor Center, and Access Roads:** Closed for bridge replacement and trail rehab (Summer 2025).
- **Old Mine Road:** Possible delays due to bridge repairs (single-lane traffic).
- **Main Street Walpack Bridge:** Closed due to structural damage.

### Appalachian Trail (NJ Section)
- **Trail Closures:** Some sections may remain closed post-Hurricane Helene. Check the [ATC website](https://appalachiantrail.org/trail-updates/) for up-to-date info.
- **Wildlife:** Black bears frequenting certain areas; follow all food storage and safety regulations.

---
## 3. Visitor Centers & Accessibility

### Delaware Water Gap
- **Bushkill Meeting Center:** Accessible building and bathrooms, open most days in summer.
  - Contact: 570-426-2452 | dewa_interpretation@nps.gov

### Appalachian Trail
- No NPS visitor center in NJ; main centers are in VA/WV/ME. For local info, contact the Appalachian Trail Conservancy.

---
## 4. Campgrounds for Overnight Stays

### Delaware Water Gap
- **Dingmans Campground:** ADA restrooms, accessible campsites, accessible camp store. [More info](https://www.dingmanscampground.com/)
- **Mohican Outdoor Center:** Group/tent sites, some amenities, call for accessibility details. [More info](https://www.outdoors.org/lodging-camping/lodges/mohican)
- **Rivers Bend Group Campground:** Handicap accessible, gravel paths, group sites.
- **Valley View Group Campground:** Site One is handicap accessible.
- **Worthington State Forest Campground:** 78 sites, some group sites with bear-proof lockers, call for accessibility.

---
## 5. Astronomy/Night Hike Events (July 2025)

- **No official astronomy or night hike events are currently scheduled** in these parks for July 2025. You may need to organize your own event or coordinate with park staff for a special program.

---
## 6. Logistics, Accessibility, and Safety Considerations

- **Accessibility:** Choose Bushkill Meeting Center as your main hub for accessible facilities. Select group campsites with ADA access (Rivers Bend, Valley View, Dingmans).
- **Safety:** Monitor trail and road closures, especially around Dingmans Falls and Old Mine Road. Prepare for possible bear encounters (especially on the Appalachian Trail).
- **Permits:** Contact the park for any special use permits required for group night events or astronomy gatherings.
- **Lighting:** Use red lights for stargazing to preserve night vision.
- **Restrooms:** Accessible restrooms available at Bushkill Meeting Center and Dingmans Campground.
- **Parking:** Confirm accessible parking at your chosen visitor center and campground.
- **Weather:** July is warm and humid; prepare for rain and insects.

---
## 7. Next Steps

1. **Contact Park Staff:** Coordinate with Delaware Water Gap rangers for event approval, accessibility support, and possible ranger-led astronomy programs.
2. **Reserve Accessible Campgrounds:** Book group sites at Dingmans, Rivers Bend, or Valley View (site one).
3. **Promote Event:** Highlight accessibility features, safety protocols, and stargazing etiquette.
4. **Prepare Materials:** Provide accessible maps, event schedules, and safety information.

Would you like a sample event schedule or assistance contacting park staff for special accommodations or permits?

Here’s a detailed plan for an accessible Astronomy and Night Hike Event in New Jersey national parks for July 2025, focusing on parks that offer both hiking and stargazing:

---
## 1. Recommended Parks in New Jersey

### Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area (DEWA)
- **Activities:** Hiking, stargazing, camping, paddling, wildlife watching.
- **Accessibility:** Bushkill Meeting Center (visitor center) and several campgrounds have accessible facilities.
- **Website:** [DEWA NPS](https://www.nps.gov/dewa/index.htm)

### Great Egg Harbor River (GREG)
- **Activities:** Hiking, stargazing, camping, paddling, birdwatching.
- **Note:** Local jurisdictions administer lands; check with Atlantic County Parks for accessibility details.
- **Website:** [Great Egg Harbor NPS](https://www.nps.gov/greg/index.htm)

### Appalachian National Scenic Trail (APPA) – NJ Section
- **Activities:** Hiking, stargazing, camping.
- **Note:** Some trail closures may persist due to storm damage; check for updates.
- **Website:** [Appalachian Trail NJ](https://www.nps.gov/appa/index.htm)

---
## 2. Current Alerts & Closures (July 2025)

### Delaware Water Gap
- **Dingmans Falls Trail, Visitor Center, and Access Roads:** Closed for bridge replacement and trail rehab (Summer 2025).
- **Old Mine Road:** Possible delays due to bridge repairs (single-lane traffic).
- **Main Street Walpack Bridge:** Closed due to structural damage.

### Appalachian Trail (NJ Section)
- **Trail Closures:** Some sections may remain closed post-Hurricane Helene. Check the [ATC website](https://appalachiantrail.org/trail-updates/) for up-to-date info.
- **Wildlife:** Black bears frequenting certain areas; follow all food storage and safety regulations.

---
## 3. Visitor Centers & Accessibility

### Delaware Water Gap
- **Bushkill Meeting Center:** Accessible building and bathrooms, open most days in summer.
  - Contact: 570-426-2452 | dewa_interpretation@nps.gov

### Appalachian Trail
- No NPS visitor center in NJ; main centers are in VA/WV/ME. For local info, contact the Appalachian Trail Conservancy.

---
## 4. Campgrounds for Overnight Stays

### Delaware Water Gap
- **Dingmans Campground:** ADA restrooms, accessible campsites, accessible camp store. [More info](https://www.dingmanscampground.com/)
- **Mohican Outdoor Center:** Group/tent sites, some amenities, call for accessibility details. [More info](https://www.outdoors.org/lodging-camping/lodges/mohican)
- **Rivers Bend Group Campground:** Handicap accessible, gravel paths, group sites.
- **Valley View Group Campground:** Site One is handicap accessible.
- **Worthington State Forest Campground:** 78 sites, some group sites with bear-proof lockers, call for accessibility.

---
## 5. Astronomy/Night Hike Events (July 2025)

- **No official astronomy or night hike events are currently scheduled** in these parks for July 2025. You may need to organize your own event or coordinate with park staff for a special program.

---
## 6. Logistics, Accessibility, and Safety Considerations

- **Accessibility:** Choose Bushkill Meeting Center as your main hub for accessible facilities. Select group campsites with ADA access (Rivers Bend, Valley View, Dingmans).
- **Safety:** Monitor trail and road closures, especially around Dingmans Falls and Old Mine Road. Prepare for possible bear encounters (especially on the Appalachian Trail).
- **Permits:** Contact the park for any special use permits required for group night events or astronomy gatherings.
- **Lighting:** Use red lights for stargazing to preserve night vision.
- **Restrooms:** Accessible restrooms available at Bushkill Meeting Center and Dingmans Campground.
- **Parking:** Confirm accessible parking at your chosen visitor center and campground.
- **Weather:** July is warm and humid; prepare for rain and insects.

---
## 7. Next Steps

1. **Contact Park Staff:** Coordinate with Delaware Water Gap rangers for event approval, accessibility support, and possible ranger-led astronomy programs.
2. **Reserve Accessible Campgrounds:** Book group sites at Dingmans, Rivers Bend, or Valley View (site one).
3. **Promote Event:** Highlight accessibility features, safety protocols, and stargazing etiquette.
4. **Prepare Materials:** Provide accessible maps, event schedules, and safety information.

final_response:
Here is a comprehensive emergency preparedness and support guide for your summer trip to Yellowstone National Park (July 10–15, 2025):

1. Activities Confirmation
- Yellowstone National Park offers both hiking and camping as primary activities. You’ll find a wide range of trails and multiple campgrounds throughout the park.

2. Current Alerts & Hazards (as of June 2025)
- Vehicle Entrance Reservation Not Needed: You only need an entrance pass (can be purchased in advance or at the gate); no vehicle reservations required.
- Daily Fishing Closures: Due to low water and warm temps, the Madison, Firehole, and parts of the Gibbon Rivers close to fishing daily at 2 p.m. until sunrise.
- Biscuit Basin Closure: The Biscuit Basin area (north of Old Faithful) is closed due to a hydrothermal explosion hazard. The parking lot, boardwalk, and Firehole River at Biscuit Basin are inaccessible until further notice.
- No park-wide closures or emergency alerts currently affect hiking or camping, but always check for updates before and during your trip: Yellowstone Alerts Page.

3. Main Visitor Centers & Hours
These are your best resources for information, help, and emergency support:
- Albright Visitor Center (Mammoth Hot Springs): Open daily 8:00 AM – 6:00 PM. Phone: 307-344-7381. Free Wi-Fi available.
- Canyon Visitor Education Center (Canyon Village): Open daily 8:00 AM – 6:00 PM.
- Fishing Bridge Visitor Center: Open daily 8:00 AM – 6:00 PM.
- Grant Visitor Center (Grant Village): Open daily 8:00 AM – 6:00 PM.
- Old Faithful Visitor Education Center: Open daily 8:00 AM – 8:00 PM.
- Madison Information Station: Open daily 9:00 AM – 4:30 PM.
- West Yellowstone Visitor Information Center (outside park, in West Yellowstone, MT): Open daily 8:00 AM – 8:00 PM. Phone: 406-646-7701.
All centers provide park info, emergency contacts, ranger assistance, and up-to-date safety bulletins.

4. Campgrounds & Backup Options
Most Yellowstone campgrounds require reservations. Here are the main options for summer 2025:
- Bridge Bay Campground: 432 sites, near Yellowstone Lake. $33/night. Reservations required.
- Canyon Campground: 273 sites, near Canyon Village. $39/night. Reservations required.
- Fishing Bridge RV Park: 310 RV-only sites with hookups. $89/night. No tents allowed. Reservations required.
- Grant Village Campground: 430 sites, near Grant Village. $39/night. Reservations required.
- Madison Campground: 276 sites, near Madison Junction. $33/night. Reservations required.
- Mammoth Campground: 85 sites, near Mammoth Hot Springs. $25/night. Reservations required April–October.
- Indian Creek Campground: 70 sites, quieter/primitive. $20/night. Reservations required.
- Lewis Lake Campground: 85 sites, near Lewis Lake. $20/night. Reservations required.
- Norris Campground: Closed for the foreseeable future.
- Pebble Creek Campground: Closed for 2025 due to flood damage.

Reservation Links:
- Yellowstone National Park Lodges (for most campgrounds): https://secure.yellowstonenationalparklodges.com/booking/lodging
- Recreation.gov (for Indian Creek, Lewis Lake, Mammoth): https://www.recreation.gov/

5. Safety & Emergency Tips
- Weather: Summer days are warm (70–80°F), but nights can be cold, even freezing at higher elevations. Pack layers and rain gear.
- Wildlife: Store all food and scented items in bear-proof lockers. Never approach wildlife.
- Closures: Check for last-minute alerts at visitor centers or the official Yellowstone website.
- Emergency Contacts: Rangers are available at all visitor centers. For emergencies, dial 911 (cell service is limited in the park).

Summary Checklist:
- Confirm your campground reservation.
- Check the latest alerts before and during your trip.
- Know the locations and hours of visitor centers for help and information.
- Prepare for variable weather and wildlife safety.
- Have backup campground options in case of closures.

Have a safe and enjoyable Yellowstone adventure! If you need more details on specific campgrounds, hiking trails, or emergency procedures, let me know.

Here is a comprehensive emergency preparedness and support guide for your summer trip to Yellowstone National Park (July 10–15, 2025):

1. Activities Confirmation
- Yellowstone National Park offers both hiking and camping as primary activities. You’ll find a wide range of trails and multiple campgrounds throughout the park.

2. Current Alerts & Hazards (as of June 2025)
- Vehicle Entrance Reservation Not Needed: You only need an entrance pass (can be purchased in advance or at the gate); no vehicle reservations required.
- Daily Fishing Closures: Due to low water and warm temps, the Madison, Firehole, and parts of the Gibbon Rivers close to fishing daily at 2 p.m. until sunrise.
- Biscuit Basin Closure: The Biscuit Basin area (north of Old Faithful) is closed due to a hydrothermal explosion hazard. The parking lot, boardwalk, and Firehole River at Biscuit Basin are inaccessible until further notice.
- No park-wide closures or emergency alerts currently affect hiking or camping, but always check for updates before and during your trip: Yellowstone Alerts Page.

3. Main Visitor Centers & Hours
These are your best resources for information, help, and emergency support:
- Albright Visitor Center (Mammoth Hot Springs): Open daily 8:00 AM – 6:00 PM. Phone: 307-344-7381. Free Wi-Fi available.
- Canyon Visitor Education Center (Canyon Village): Open daily 8:00 AM – 6:00 PM.
- Fishing Bridge Visitor Center: Open daily 8:00 AM – 6:00 PM.
- Grant Visitor Center (Grant Village): Open daily 8:00 AM – 6:00 PM.
- Old Faithful Visitor Education Center: Open daily 8:00 AM – 8:00 PM.
- Madison Information Station: Open daily 9:00 AM – 4:30 PM.
- West Yellowstone Visitor Information Center (outside park, in West Yellowstone, MT): Open daily 8:00 AM – 8:00 PM. Phone: 406-646-7701.
All centers provide park info, emergency contacts, ranger assistance, and up-to-date safety bulletins.

4. Campgrounds & Backup Options
Most Yellowstone campgrounds require reservations. Here are the main options for summer 2025:
- Bridge Bay Campground: 432 sites, near Yellowstone Lake. $33/night. Reservations required.
- Canyon Campground: 273 sites, near Canyon Village. $39/night. Reservations required.
- Fishing Bridge RV Park: 310 RV-only sites with hookups. $89/night. No tents allowed. Reservations required.
- Grant Village Campground: 430 sites, near Grant Village. $39/night. Reservations required.
- Madison Campground: 276 sites, near Madison Junction. $33/night. Reservations required.
- Mammoth Campground: 85 sites, near Mammoth Hot Springs. $25/night. Reservations required April–October.
- Indian Creek Campground: 70 sites, quieter/primitive. $20/night. Reservations required.
- Lewis Lake Campground: 85 sites, near Lewis Lake. $20/night. Reservations required.
- Norris Campground: Closed for the foreseeable future.
- Pebble Creek Campground: Closed for 2025 due to flood damage.

Reservation Links:
- Yellowstone National Park Lodges (for most campgrounds): https://secure.yellowstonenationalparklodges.com/booking/lodging
- Recreation.gov (for Indian Creek, Lewis Lake, Mammoth): https://www.recreation.gov/

5. Safety & Emergency Tips
- Weather: Summer days are warm (70–80°F), but nights can be cold, even freezing at higher elevations. Pack layers and rain gear.
- Wildlife: Store all food and scented items in bear-proof lockers. Never approach wildlife.
- Closures: Check for last-minute alerts at visitor centers or the official Yellowstone website.
- Emergency Contacts: Rangers are available at all visitor centers. For emergencies, dial 911 (cell service is limited in the park).

Summary Checklist:
- Confirm your campground reservation.
- Check the latest alerts before and during your trip.
- Know the locations and hours of visitor centers for help and information.
- Prepare for variable weather and wildlife safety.
- Have backup campground options in case of closures.

Have a safe and enjoyable Yellowstone adventure! If you need more details on specific campgrounds, hiking trails, or emergency procedures, let me know.

final_response:
Here’s a detailed itinerary for a Tennessee National Park Music and Cultural Festival Tour for July–August 2025, focusing on parks with music/cultural activities and camping options. While no specific live music or festival events are currently scheduled in the NPS system for these dates, the parks below offer rich cultural programming, exhibits, and immersive experiences, and are known for hosting seasonal music/cultural events. This itinerary includes park details, current alerts, visitor centers, campgrounds, and relevant notes for your group.

---

## 1. Great Smoky Mountains National Park (GRSM)
- **Why Visit:** Renowned for Appalachian mountain culture, live music (seasonal), historic structures, and cultural exhibits.
- **Park Details:** [NPS Smokies](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/index.htm)
- **Cultural Highlights:** Cades Cove features historic buildings, living history, and often hosts bluegrass/folk music demonstrations and cultural programs.
- **Alerts:**
  - Park Headquarters Road closed through September 2025 (use Sugarlands Visitor Center for access).
  - Cades Cove Loop Road closed to vehicles every Wednesday (June 18–Sept 24) for pedestrian/cyclist enjoyment.
  - Some secondary roads and areas closed due to construction or damage.
- **Visitor Centers:**
  - Cades Cove Visitor Center (Cable Mill Road, Townsend, TN 37882)
  - Kuwohi (Clingmans Dome) Visitor Center
- **Campgrounds:**
  - Abrams Creek, Balsam Mountain, Big Creek, Cades Cove, Cataloochee (all require reservations; see [campground info](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/campgrounds.htm))
- **Notes:** Check the park’s calendar closer to your visit for updated music/cultural event listings.

---

## 2. Big South Fork National River & Recreation Area (BISO)
- **Why Visit:** Offers cultural exhibits, historic mining community (Blue Heron), and often hosts Appalachian music and cultural events.
- **Park Details:** [NPS Big South Fork](https://www.nps.gov/biso/index.htm)
- **Cultural Highlights:** Blue Heron Mining Community (interpretive audio, historic structures), ranger programs, and seasonal events.
- **Alerts:** No major alerts currently affecting visitor experience.
- **Visitor Centers:**
  - Bandy Creek Visitor Center (Oneida, TN)
  - Blue Heron Interpretive Center (Strunk, KY)
  - Crossville and Helenwood Visitor Centers
- **Campgrounds:**
  - Bandy Creek (large, modern, group options)
  - Alum Ford (primitive)
  - Blue Heron (electric/water hookups)
  - Bear Creek (horse camping)
- **Notes:** Check with the visitor center for scheduled music/cultural programs during your visit.

---

## 3. Andrew Johnson National Historic Site (ANJO)
- **Why Visit:** Deep dive into post-Civil War history, museum exhibits, and cultural programming.
- **Park Details:** [NPS Andrew Johnson](https://www.nps.gov/anjo/index.htm)
- **Cultural Highlights:** Museum, original tailor shop, historic homes, and frequent interpretive programs.
- **Alerts:** No morning guided tours on July 11, 2025, due to education groups.
- **Visitor Center:** 101 North College Street, Greeneville, TN 37743
- **Campgrounds:** No NPS campgrounds onsite; consider nearby state parks or combine with Smokies/Big South Fork camping.
- **Notes:** Great for history buffs and those interested in American government and Reconstruction.

---

## 4. Chickamauga & Chattanooga National Military Park (CHCH)
- **Why Visit:** Civil War history, living history demonstrations, museum exhibits, and cultural interpretation.
- **Park Details:** [NPS Chickamauga & Chattanooga](https://www.nps.gov/chch/index.htm)
- **Cultural Highlights:** Living history, historic weapons demonstrations, museum, and interpretive programs.
- **Alerts:** No major alerts currently affecting visitor experience.
- **Visitor Center:** 3370 LaFayette Road, Fort Oglethorpe, GA 30742 (just south of Chattanooga, TN)
- **Campgrounds:** No NPS campgrounds onsite; nearby private/state campgrounds available.
- **Notes:** Check for special anniversary or commemorative events.

---

## 5. Cumberland Gap National Historical Park (CUGA)
- **Why Visit:** Gateway to the West, pioneer history, cultural exhibits, and Appalachian heritage.
- **Park Details:** [NPS Cumberland Gap](https://www.nps.gov/cuga/index.htm)
- **Cultural Highlights:** Hensley Settlement, cave tours, museum exhibits, and ranger-led programs.
- **Alerts:** No major alerts currently affecting visitor experience.

Here’s a detailed itinerary for a Tennessee National Park Music and Cultural Festival Tour for July–August 2025, focusing on parks with music/cultural activities and camping options. While no specific live music or festival events are currently scheduled in the NPS system for these dates, the parks below offer rich cultural programming, exhibits, and immersive experiences, and are known for hosting seasonal music/cultural events. This itinerary includes park details, current alerts, visitor centers, campgrounds, and relevant notes for your group.

---

## 1. Great Smoky Mountains National Park (GRSM)
- **Why Visit:** Renowned for Appalachian mountain culture, live music (seasonal), historic structures, and cultural exhibits.
- **Park Details:** [NPS Smokies](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/index.htm)
- **Cultural Highlights:** Cades Cove features historic buildings, living history, and often hosts bluegrass/folk music demonstrations and cultural programs.
- **Alerts:**
  - Park Headquarters Road closed through September 2025 (use Sugarlands Visitor Center for access).
  - Cades Cove Loop Road closed to vehicles every Wednesday (June 18–Sept 24) for pedestrian/cyclist enjoyment.
  - Some secondary roads and areas closed due to construction or damage.
- **Visitor Centers:**
  - Cades Cove Visitor Center (Cable Mill Road, Townsend, TN 37882)
  - Kuwohi (Clingmans Dome) Visitor Center
- **Campgrounds:**
  - Abrams Creek, Balsam Mountain, Big Creek, Cades Cove, Cataloochee (all require reservations; see [campground info](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/campgrounds.htm))
- **Notes:** Check the park’s calendar closer to your visit for updated music/cultural event listings.

---

## 2. Big South Fork National River & Recreation Area (BISO)
- **Why Visit:** Offers cultural exhibits, historic mining community (Blue Heron), and often hosts Appalachian music and cultural events.
- **Park Details:** [NPS Big South Fork](https://www.nps.gov/biso/index.htm)
- **Cultural Highlights:** Blue Heron Mining Community (interpretive audio, historic structures), ranger programs, and seasonal events.
- **Alerts:** No major alerts currently affecting visitor experience.
- **Visitor Centers:**
  - Bandy Creek Visitor Center (Oneida, TN)
  - Blue Heron Interpretive Center (Strunk, KY)
  - Crossville and Helenwood Visitor Centers
- **Campgrounds:**
  - Bandy Creek (large, modern, group options)
  - Alum Ford (primitive)
  - Blue Heron (electric/water hookups)
  - Bear Creek (horse camping)
- **Notes:** Check with the visitor center for scheduled music/cultural programs during your visit.

---

## 3. Andrew Johnson National Historic Site (ANJO)
- **Why Visit:** Deep dive into post-Civil War history, museum exhibits, and cultural programming.
- **Park Details:** [NPS Andrew Johnson](https://www.nps.gov/anjo/index.htm)
- **Cultural Highlights:** Museum, original tailor shop, historic homes, and frequent interpretive programs.
- **Alerts:** No morning guided tours on July 11, 2025, due to education groups.
- **Visitor Center:** 101 North College Street, Greeneville, TN 37743
- **Campgrounds:** No NPS campgrounds onsite; consider nearby state parks or combine with Smokies/Big South Fork camping.
- **Notes:** Great for history buffs and those interested in American government and Reconstruction.

---

## 4. Chickamauga & Chattanooga National Military Park (CHCH)
- **Why Visit:** Civil War history, living history demonstrations, museum exhibits, and cultural interpretation.
- **Park Details:** [NPS Chickamauga & Chattanooga](https://www.nps.gov/chch/index.htm)
- **Cultural Highlights:** Living history, historic weapons demonstrations, museum, and interpretive programs.
- **Alerts:** No major alerts currently affecting visitor experience.
- **Visitor Center:** 3370 LaFayette Road, Fort Oglethorpe, GA 30742 (just south of Chattanooga, TN)
- **Campgrounds:** No NPS campgrounds onsite; nearby private/state campgrounds available.
- **Notes:** Check for special anniversary or commemorative events.

---

## 5. Cumberland Gap National Historical Park (CUGA)
- **Why Visit:** Gateway to the West, pioneer history, cultural exhibits, and Appalachian heritage.
- **Park Details:** [NPS Cumberland Gap](https://www.nps.gov/cuga/index.htm)
- **Cultural Highlights:** Hensley Settlement, cave tours, museum exhibits, and ranger-led programs.
- **Alerts:** No major alerts currently affecting visitor experience.

Here is a detailed plan for an Accessible Gardening and Pollinator Education Weekend for families in Midwest national parks, focusing on three top options: Cuyahoga Valley National Park (OH), Apostle Islands National Lakeshore (WI), and Badlands National Park (SD). The plan includes park recommendations, accessibility details, visitor centers, campgrounds, alerts, and events for June 21-22, 2025.

## 1. Cuyahoga Valley National Park (Ohio)
**Website:** [Cuyahoga Valley NP](https://www.nps.gov/cuva/index.htm)  
**Location:** Peninsula, OH (near Cleveland and Akron)  
**Description:** A refuge for native plants and wildlife, with forests, rolling hills, and open farmlands. The park is known for its accessibility and family-friendly atmosphere.

### Accessibility & Facilities
- The park is open 24/7, with some areas closed from dusk to morning.
- Boston Mill Visitor Center is a good starting point: 6947 Riverview Road, Peninsula, OH 44264.
- No specific gardening or pollinator exhibits at visitor centers, but the park has a strong focus on native habitats and citizen science.

Here is a detailed plan for an Accessible Gardening and Pollinator Education Weekend for families in Midwest national parks, focusing on three top options: Cuyahoga Valley National Park (OH), Apostle Islands National Lakeshore (WI), and Badlands National Park (SD). The plan includes park recommendations, accessibility details, visitor centers, campgrounds, alerts, and events for June 21-22, 2025.

---

## 1. Cuyahoga Valley National Park (Ohio)
**Website:** [Cuyahoga Valley NP](https://www.nps.gov/cuva/index.htm)  
**Location:** Peninsula, OH (near Cleveland and Akron)  
**Description:** A refuge for native plants and wildlife, with forests, rolling hills, and open farmlands. The park is known for its accessibility and family-friendly atmosphere.

### Accessibility & Facilities
- The park is open 24/7, with some areas closed from dusk to morning.
- Boston Mill Visitor Center is a good starting point: 6947 Riverview Road, Peninsula, OH 44264.
- No specific gardening or pollinator exhibits at visitor centers, but the park has a strong focus on native habitats and citizen science.
- No NPS-operated campgrounds, but nearby private and state campgrounds are available. (No accessible NPS campgrounds found.)
- Wheelchair-accessible trails and facilities are available throughout the park.

### Current Alerts (as of June 2025)
- Select restrooms are closed until further notice.
- Expect crowding on weekends and warm days (10am–3pm).
- Vehicle break-ins have increased—do not leave valuables in your car.
- Some areas (former golf course property) are closed for remediation.

### Events (June 21-22, 2025)
- No specific gardening or pollinator events listed for this weekend, but the park frequently hosts citizen science and nature education programs. Check closer to your visit for updates.

---

## 2. Apostle Islands National Lakeshore (Wisconsin)
**Website:** [Apostle Islands NL](https://www.nps.gov/apis/index.htm)  
**Location:** Bayfield, WI (Lake Superior)  
**Description:** 21 islands and a scenic shoreline, known for natural beauty, lighthouses, and wildlife. Great for families interested in nature and pollinators.

### Accessibility & Facilities
- Open year-round; most areas accessible by water.
- No specific gardening or pollinator exhibits at visitor centers.
- No NPS-operated accessible campgrounds found; most camping is backcountry or group camping on the islands, which may not be suitable for all accessibility needs.
- Visitor center: 415 Washington Avenue, Bayfield, WI 54814.

### Current Alerts (as of June 2025)
- Devil’s Island Marina and campsite closed for construction (summer 2025).
- Meyers Beach parking fees are digital only.
- Some closures on Devils Island, Sand Island, and Stockton Island trails.
- Black bears are present—follow safety guidelines.

### Events (June 21-22, 2025)
- No specific gardening or pollinator events listed for this weekend.

---

## 3. Badlands National Park (South Dakota)
**Website:** [Badlands NP](https://www.nps.gov/badl/index.htm)  
**Location:** Interior, SD  
**Description:** Famous for dramatic landscapes, prairie ecosystems, and wildlife. The park protects mixed-grass prairie, important for pollinators.

### Accessibility & Facilities
- Open year-round.
- Cedar Pass Campground: 96 sites, 2 fully wheelchair-accessible campsites, accessible restrooms, and level sites. [Reserve here](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/10288228?tab=campsites)
- Sage Creek Campground: Primitive, free, accessible vault toilets, rough terrain.
- No specific gardening or pollinator exhibits at visitor centers.

### Current Alerts (as of June 2025)
- Conata Picnic Ground closed for construction.
- Do not rely on GPS for navigation—use official directions.

### Events (June 21-22, 2025)
- No specific gardening or pollinator events listed for this weekend.

---

### Best Park for Accessibility & Family Experience
**Cuyahoga Valley National Park** stands out for its accessibility, family-friendly trails, and educational focus on native habitats. final_response:
Here’s a detailed plan for an Accessible Birding and Nature Interpretation Weekend in Wisconsin national parks for June 14–15, 2025, focusing on accessibility, birdwatching, and up-to-date alerts:

—
## 1. Park Options in Wisconsin
The following national parks in Wisconsin offer birdwatching and accessible activities:

### Apostle Islands National Lakeshore (APIS)
- Stunning islands, lighthouses, and shoreline birdwatching.
- Accessible visitor centers and interpretive exhibits.
- Website: [Apostle Islands NPS](https://www.nps.gov/apis/index.htm)

### Saint Croix National Scenic Riverway (SACN)
- Forested river landscapes, excellent for birdwatching.
- Accessible visitor centers and river overlooks.
- Website: [Saint Croix NPS](https://www.nps.gov/sacn/index.htm)

### Ice Age National Scenic Trail (IATR)
- 1,200-mile trail with birdwatching opportunities.
- Some segments may be accessible; check local trail conditions.
- Website: [Ice Age Trail NPS](https://www.nps.gov/iatr/index.htm)

### North Country National Scenic Trail (NOCO)
- Long-distance trail with birdwatching.
- Accessibility varies by segment; check local trail alerts.
- Website: [North Country Trail NPS](https://www.nps.gov/noco/index.htm)

—
## 2. Current Alerts Affecting Accessibility

### Apostle Islands National Lakeshore
- **Devil’s Island Marina Construction**: Marina and campsite closed summer 2025; possible impacts at Little Sand Bay.
- **Ongoing Closures**: Devils Island dock/campsites, West Bay Club (Sand Island), and part of Stockton Island trail closed.
- **Bear Alert**: Black bears present; follow food storage guidelines.
- **Meyers Beach Parking**: Digital payments only.
- [More info & updates](https://www.nps.gov/apis/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)

### Saint Croix National Scenic Riverway
- **Bear Activity**: Increased bear activity along Namekagon River; store food properly.
- [Bear safety info](https://www.nps.gov/articles/bearsafetyfood.htm)

### Ice Age & North Country Trails
- **Trail Conditions Vary**: Check [Ice Age Trail Alerts](https://iceagetrail.maps.arcgis.com/apps/opsdashboard/index.html#/5cb8ca63f0e447dea9dc29afb5ed12e6) and [North Country Trail Alerts](https://northcountrytrail.org/the-trail/trail-alerts/) for up-to-date accessibility and closures.

—
## 3. Accessible Visitor Centers

### Apostle Islands
- **Bayfield Headquarters**
  - 415 Washington Ave, Bayfield, WI 54814
  - Open June 14–15: 9:00AM–4:30PM
  - Accessible exhibits, park film, bookstore.
- **Little Sand Bay Visitor Center**
  - 32660 Little Sand Bay Rd, Bayfield, WI 54814
  - Open June 14–15: 9:00AM–5:00PM
  - Accessible exhibits, orientation, kayak safety.

### Saint Croix National Scenic Riverway
- **Namekagon River Visitor Center**
  - W5483 U.S. Highway 63, Trego, WI 54888
  - Open June 14–15: 10:00AM–5:00PM
  - Accessible exhibits, trip planning, park film.
- **St. Croix River Visitor Center**
  - 401 North Hamilton St., St. Croix Falls, WI 54024
  - Open June 14–15: 10:00AM–5:00PM
  - Accessible exhibits, trip planning, park film.

—
## 4. Birding & Nature Interpretation Events (June 14–15, 2025)
- No scheduled birding or nature interpretation events were found for these dates. However, both Apostle Islands and Saint Croix Riverway offer ranger-led programs and self-guided interpretive trails—check with visitor centers for up-to-date offerings closer to your visit.

—
## 5. Sample Itinerary

### Saturday, June 14
- **Morning**: Start at Bayfield Headquarters Visitor Center (Apostle Islands) for orientation and accessibility info.
- **Midday**: Visit Little Sand Bay Visitor Center for interpretive exhibits and accessible shoreline birdwatching.
- **Afternoon**: Explore accessible trails or overlooks (check with rangers for current accessible routes).
- **Evening**: Optional sunset birdwatching at accessible shoreline spots.

### Sunday, June 15
- **Morning**: Visit Namekagon River Visitor Center (Saint Croix Riverway) for exhibits and trip planning.
- **Midday**: Enjoy accessible river overlooks

Here’s a detailed plan for an Accessible Birding and Nature Interpretation Weekend in Wisconsin national parks for June 14–15, 2025, focusing on accessibility, birdwatching, and up-to-date alerts:

—
## 1. Park Options in Wisconsin
The following national parks in Wisconsin offer birdwatching and accessible activities:

### Apostle Islands National Lakeshore (APIS)
- Stunning islands, lighthouses, and shoreline birdwatching.
- Accessible visitor centers and interpretive exhibits.
- Website: [Apostle Islands NPS](https://www.nps.gov/apis/index.htm)

### Saint Croix National Scenic Riverway (SACN)
- Forested river landscapes, excellent for birdwatching.
- Accessible visitor centers and river overlooks.
- Website: [Saint Croix NPS](https://www.nps.gov/sacn/index.htm)

### Ice Age National Scenic Trail (IATR)
- 1,200-mile trail with birdwatching opportunities.
- Some segments may be accessible; check local trail conditions.
- Website: [Ice Age Trail NPS](https://www.nps.gov/iatr/index.htm)

### North Country National Scenic Trail (NOCO)
- Long-distance trail with birdwatching.
- Accessibility varies by segment; check local trail alerts.
- Website: [North Country Trail NPS](https://www.nps.gov/noco/index.htm)

—
## 2. Current Alerts Affecting Accessibility

### Apostle Islands National Lakeshore
- **Devil’s Island Marina Construction**: Marina and campsite closed summer 2025; possible impacts at Little Sand Bay.
- **Ongoing Closures**: Devils Island dock/campsites, West Bay Club (Sand Island), and part of Stockton Island trail closed.
- **Bear Alert**: Black bears present; follow food storage guidelines.
- **Meyers Beach Parking**: Digital payments only.
- [More info & updates](https://www.nps.gov/apis/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)

### Saint Croix National Scenic Riverway
- **Bear Activity**: Increased bear activity along Namekagon River; store food properly.
- [Bear safety info](https://www.nps.gov/articles/bearsafetyfood.htm)

### Ice Age & North Country Trails
- **Trail Conditions Vary**: Check [Ice Age Trail Alerts](https://iceagetrail.maps.arcgis.com/apps/opsdashboard/index.html#/5cb8ca63f0e447dea9dc29afb5ed12e6) and [North Country Trail Alerts](https://northcountrytrail.org/the-trail/trail-alerts/) for up-to-date accessibility and closures.

—
## 3. Accessible Visitor Centers

### Apostle Islands
- **Bayfield Headquarters**
  - 415 Washington Ave, Bayfield, WI 54814
  - Open June 14–15: 9:00AM–4:30PM
  - Accessible exhibits, park film, bookstore.
- **Little Sand Bay Visitor Center**
  - 32660 Little Sand Bay Rd, Bayfield, WI 54814
  - Open June 14–15: 9:00AM–5:00PM
  - Accessible exhibits, orientation, kayak safety.

### Saint Croix National Scenic Riverway
- **Namekagon River Visitor Center**
  - W5483 U.S. Highway 63, Trego, WI 54888
  - Open June 14–15: 10:00AM–5:00PM
  - Accessible exhibits, trip planning, park film.
- **St. Croix River Visitor Center**
  - 401 North Hamilton St., St. Croix Falls, WI 54024
  - Open June 14–15: 10:00AM–5:00PM
  - Accessible exhibits, trip planning, park film.

—
## 4. Birding & Nature Interpretation Events (June 14–15, 2025)
- No scheduled birding or nature interpretation events were found for these dates. However, both Apostle Islands and Saint Croix Riverway offer ranger-led programs and self-guided interpretive trails—check with visitor centers for up-to-date offerings closer to your visit.

—
## 5. Sample Itinerary

### Saturday, June 14
- **Morning**: Start at Bayfield Headquarters Visitor Center (Apostle Islands) for orientation and accessibility info.
- **Midday**: Visit Little Sand Bay Visitor Center for interpretive exhibits and accessible shoreline birdwatching.
- **Afternoon**: Explore accessible trails or overlooks (check with rangers for current accessible routes).
- **Evening**: Optional sunset birdwatching at accessible shoreline spots.

### Sunday, June 15
- **Morning**: Visit Namekagon River Visitor Center (Saint Croix Riverway) for exhibits and trip planning.
- **Midday**: Enjoy accessible river overlooks

final_response:
Here is a comprehensive planning guide for your National Park Wellness and Mindful Walking Retreat in the Great Smoky Mountains National Park (Tennessee side) for July 2025:

---

### 1. Park Overview & Suitability

**Great Smoky Mountains National Park**
- Straddles Tennessee and North Carolina; most visited national park in the U.S.
- Renowned for biodiversity, ancient mountains, and Appalachian culture.
- Activities: Hiking (front- and backcountry), camping, guided tours, wildlife watching, and more.
- Weather: Elevations range from 875 to 6,643 feet; temperatures can vary by 10–20°F from base to summit.
- Directions: Main entrances in Gatlinburg, TN; Townsend, TN; and Cherokee, NC.
- Website: [Great Smoky Mountains National Park](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/index.htm)

---

Here is a comprehensive planning guide for your National Park Wellness and Mindful Walking Retreat in the Great Smoky Mountains National Park (Tennessee side) for July 2025:

---

### 1. Park Overview & Suitability

**Great Smoky Mountains National Park**
- Straddles Tennessee and North Carolina; most visited national park in the U.S.
- Renowned for biodiversity, ancient mountains, and Appalachian culture.
- Activities: Hiking (front- and backcountry), camping, guided tours, wildlife watching, and more.
- Weather: Elevations range from 875 to 6,643 feet; temperatures can vary by 10–20°F from base to summit.
- Directions: Main entrances in Gatlinburg, TN; Townsend, TN; and Cherokee, NC.
- Website: [Great Smoky Mountains National Park](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/index.htm)

---

### 2. Current Alerts (as of July 2025)

- **Park Headquarters Road closed due to construction through September 2025.** For Gatlinburg Trail or Fighting Creek Nature Trail, park at Sugarlands Visitor Center.
- **Old NC 284 closed from Cataloochee Creek to Cataloochee Valley** (road damage).
- **Cades Cove Loop Road closed to motor vehicles every Wednesday (June 18–Sept 24).** Pedestrian/cyclist only—ideal for mindful walking!
- **Straight Fork and part of Balsam Mountain Road closed.** Balsam Mountain Campground remains accessible.
- **Parking Tag Required:** All vehicles parking for more than 15 minutes need a tag ($5/day, $15/week, $40/year). [Parking Tag Info](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/fees.htm)

---

### 3. Visitor Centers & Hours

- **Sugarlands Visitor Center (Gatlinburg, TN)**
  - Hours: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM (seasonal variations possible)
  - Address: 1420 Fighting Creek Gap Road, Gatlinburg, TN 37738
  - Phone: (865) 436-1200
  - [More Info](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/visitorcenters.htm)

- **Cades Cove Visitor Center (Townsend, TN)**
  - Hours: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM
  - Address: Cable Mill Road, Townsend, TN 37882

- **Kuwohi (Clingmans Dome) Visitor Center**
  - Hours: 9:30 AM – 6:00 PM (closed in winter)
  - Address: Clingmans Dome Road, Cherokee, NC 28719

- **Oconaluftee Visitor Center (NC side)**
  - Hours: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM
  - Address: 1194 Newfound Gap Road, Cherokee, NC 28719

---

### 4. Campgrounds (Reservations Required)

- **Elkmont Campground**
  - Closest to Sugarlands Visitor Center.
  - Open March 14 – Nov 30, 2025.
  - 211 sites, $30/night, tent & RV sites, flush toilets, potable water, no showers.
  - [Reserve Elkmont](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232487)

- **Cades Cove Campground**
  - Open year-round, 161 sites, $30/night, tent & RV, flush toilets, potable water, no showers.
  - [Reserve Cades Cove](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232488)

- **Cosby Campground**
  - 157 sites, $30/night, tent & RV, flush toilets, potable water, no showers.
  - [Reserve Cosby](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232479)

- **Group Campgrounds** (for larger retreat groups)
  - Cades Cove Group: Up to 30 people, $35–$65/night.
  - Elkmont Group: Up to 30 people, $26–$53/night.
  - [Group Reservations](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232440) (Cades Cove), [Elkmont Group](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232436)

---

final_response:
Here’s a detailed plan for an accessible canoeing and wildlife watching weekend in Minnesota national parks for June 21-22, 2025. This plan focuses on parks with the best opportunities for canoeing, wildlife watching, and accessibility, and includes alerts, campgrounds, visitor centers, and events.

---

## Top Park Choices for Accessible Canoeing & Wildlife Watching

### 1. Voyageurs National Park
- **Why Choose:** Voyageurs is renowned for its interconnected lakes, abundant wildlife, and accessible facilities. It offers accessible boat tours, visitor centers, and some accessible campsites.
- **Activities:** Canoeing, kayaking, wildlife watching (bald eagles, otters, loons, deer, and more).
- **Accessibility:** Voyageurs has accessible docks, restrooms, and visitor centers. Some boat tours are wheelchair accessible—contact the park for details and reservations.

### 2. Mississippi National River & Recreation Area
- **Why Choose:** Located in the Twin Cities, this park offers urban access to canoeing and wildlife watching, with accessible trails and visitor centers.
- **Activities:** Canoeing, birdwatching, accessible riverfront trails.
- **Accessibility:** The Mississippi River Visitor Center is accessible, and many city and regional parks along the river have accessible canoe launches and wildlife viewing areas.

### 3. St. Croix National Scenic Riverway
- **Why Choose:** The St. Croix River is a classic canoeing destination with beautiful scenery and wildlife. Some launches and visitor centers are accessible.
- **Activities:** Canoeing, kayaking, birdwatching, wildlife viewing.
- **Accessibility:** Visitor centers are accessible, but most primitive campsites are not wheelchair accessible.

---

## Current Alerts (as of June 2025)
- **Mississippi River Visitor Center Closure:** Closed Sept 9–13, 2025, for annual cleaning. Not relevant for your June dates.
- **Bear Activity (St. Croix):** Increased bear activity along the Namekagon River. Store food and scented items properly. See bear safety info: [Bear Safety](https://www.nps.gov/articles/bearsafetyfood.htm)
- **No major accessibility-impacting alerts for Voyageurs or Grand Portage as of now.**

---

## Accessible Campgrounds

### Voyageurs National Park
- **Accessible Camping:** Voyageurs offers several front-country campsites and houseboat sites with accessible features. Contact the park for specific accessible site reservations and details.
- **Reservations:** Highly recommended for accessible sites. Visit: [Voyageurs Camping Info](https://www.nps.gov/voya/planyourvisit/camping.htm) or call (218)-283-6600.

### St. Croix National Scenic Riverway
- **Primitive Campsites:** Not wheelchair accessible. Most are canoe-in only and lack ADA features.
- **Alternative:** Consider nearby state parks (e.g., William O’Brien State Park) for accessible camping and easy access to the river.

### Grand Portage National Monument
- **Fort Charlotte Backcountry Campgrounds:** Not wheelchair accessible.

---

## Visitor Centers with Accessibility

### Voyageurs National Park
- **Rainy Lake Visitor Center:** Accessible, open daily 9am–5pm.
- **Kabetogama Lake Visitor Center:** Accessible, open daily 9am–5pm.
- **Ash River Visitor Center:** Accessible, open daily 9am–5pm.
- **Crane Lake Visitor Center:** Accessible, open daily 9am–5pm.

### Mississippi National River & Recreation Area
- **Mississippi River Visitor Center:** Accessible, open daily except Mondays, 9am–5pm.

### St. Croix National Scenic Riverway
- **St. Croix River Visitor Center:** Accessible, open daily 10am–5pm (seasonal).
- **Namekagon River Visitor Center:** Accessible, open Thurs–Mon, 10am–5pm (seasonal).

### Grand Portage National Monument
- **Heritage Center:** Accessible, open daily 9am–5pm.

---

## Events (June 21-22, 2025)
- No special events are currently scheduled in these parks for your weekend. However, regular ranger programs and wildlife talks may be available—check with visitor centers upon arrival.

---

## Sample Itinerary

### Day 1: Saturday, June 21
- **Morning:** Arrive at Voyageurs National Park. Stop at Rainy Lake or Kabetogama Lake Visitor Center for maps, accessibility info, and wildlife updates.
- **Midday:** Canoe or take an accessible boat tour (reserve in advance). Watch for eagles, loons, and otters.
- **Afternoon:** Wildlife watching from accessible trails or docks. Picnic at accessible areas.
- **Evening:** Set up at an accessible campsite or nearby accessible lodging.
