final_response:
Here’s a comprehensive plan for an accessible National Park Star Party and Astronomy Night in Texas during the June 2025 new moon weekend (June 27–29, 2025). The two best national parks in Texas for stargazing and astronomy are Big Bend National Park and Padre Island National Seashore. Below you’ll find details on accessibility, current alerts, visitor centers, accessible campgrounds, and astronomy event listings for both parks.

---

## 1. Big Bend National Park

**Why Big Bend?**
- International Dark Sky Park with some of the darkest skies in the U.S.
- Regular astronomy and night sky programs (none currently scheduled for June 27–29, 2025, but check closer to the date).

### Accessibility

- **Visitor Centers:** All main visitor centers (Panther Junction, Chisos Basin, Rio Grande Village, Persimmon Gap, Castolon) have accessible facilities. Contact Panther Junction Visitor Center for detailed accessibility info: 432-477-2251, bibe_info@nps.gov.
- **Accessible Trails:** Some short, paved or boardwalk trails (e.g., Rio Grande Village Nature Trail’s first section).
- **Campgrounds:**
  - **Chisos Basin Campground:** 1 ADA site (#37), paved walkway, accessible table/grill, accessible restroom. Hilly terrain.
  - **Cottonwood Campground:** 2 fully accessible sites, flat paved surfaces, paved path to accessible vault toilet.
  - **Rio Grande Village Campground:** 1 ADA site, paved, flat, accessible restroom and water. Boardwalk trail nearby.
  - **Rio Grande Village RV Park:** Flat, paved, full hookups for RVs, accessible for mobility devices.
- **Park Entrances:** All main roads are paved and accessible by standard vehicles.

### Current Alerts (as of June 2025)
- Some road closures due to flooding (including paved road between Cottonwood Campground and Santa Elena Canyon, Hot Springs Rd, Old Maverick Rd, most dirt roads, and Boquillas Crossing).
- Chisos Basin improvement projects begin Fall 2025 (after your event).
- Panther Junction convenience store closed for remodel, but gas/diesel available.
- No drones allowed.
- Pets are restricted to developed areas and roads.

### Stargazing & Astronomy Events
- No astronomy events are currently scheduled for June 27–29, 2025. However, the park’s dark skies make it ideal for a DIY star party. Contact the park for possible ranger-led programs closer to your date.

### Campground Reservations
- All campgrounds require reservations: [Big Bend Campgrounds Info & Reservations](https://www.nps.gov/bibe/planyourvisit/camping.htm)

---

## 2. Padre Island National Seashore

**Why Padre Island?**
- Designated as an International Dark Sky Park.
- Offers beach stargazing and occasional astronomy programs (none currently scheduled for June 27–29, 2025).

### Accessibility

- **Visitor Center:** Malaquite Visitor Center is fully accessible, with accessible restrooms, ramp to the beach, and free beach wheelchair loan.
- **Campgrounds:**
  - **Malaquite Campground:** 2 accessible sites (#12, #13) near restrooms, showers, and accessible boardwalk to the beach. Paved and flat, but picnic tables are not wheelchair accessible.
  - **Bird Island Basin Campground:** Flat gravel, no designated accessible sites, but vault toilets are ramp-accessible.
- **Beach Access:** Accessible ramp from Malaquite Visitor Center to the beach; beach wheelchairs available.

### Current Alerts (as of June 2025)
- Canine distemper present—keep pets vaccinated or at home.
- Changing beach conditions—check tides and weather.
- Natural tar balls may be present on the beach.
- 4-wheel drive recommended for beach driving.

### Stargazing & Astronomy Events
- No astronomy events are currently scheduled for June 27–29, 2025. The beach is open for night sky viewing; check with the visitor center for possible last-minute programs.

### Campground Info
- All sites are first-come, first-served; arrive early for best selection.
- [Padre Island Camping Info](https://www.nps.gov/pais/planyourvisit/camping.htm)

---

## 3. Planning Tips for Accessibility

- Contact the visitor centers ahead of time for the most up-to-date accessibility information and to request accommodations.
- Bring red-light flashlights, accessible star charts, and plan for hot weather (hydration, sun protection).
- For group events, coordinate with park staff for accessible gathering locations and possible ranger support.
- For Big Bend, be aware of summer heat and limited shade; plan evening activities and bring cooling aids.

---

## 4. Contact Information

**Big Bend National Park**
- Website

Here’s a comprehensive plan for an accessible National Park Star Party and Astronomy Night in Texas during the June 2025 new moon weekend (June 27–29, 2025). The two best national parks in Texas for stargazing and astronomy are Big Bend National Park and Padre Island National Seashore. Below you’ll find details on accessibility, current alerts, visitor centers, accessible campgrounds, and astronomy event listings for both parks.

---

## 1. Big Bend National Park

**Why Big Bend?**
- International Dark Sky Park with some of the darkest skies in the U.S.
- Regular astronomy and night sky programs (none currently scheduled for June 27–29, 2025, but check closer to the date).

### Accessibility

- **Visitor Centers:** All main visitor centers (Panther Junction, Chisos Basin, Rio Grande Village, Persimmon Gap, Castolon) have accessible facilities. Contact Panther Junction Visitor Center for detailed accessibility info: 432-477-2251, bibe_info@nps.gov.
- **Accessible Trails:** Some short, paved or boardwalk trails (e.g., Rio Grande Village Nature Trail’s first section).
- **Campgrounds:**
  - **Chisos Basin Campground:** 1 ADA site (#37), paved walkway, accessible table/grill, accessible restroom. Hilly terrain.
  - **Cottonwood Campground:** 2 fully accessible sites, flat paved surfaces, paved path to accessible vault toilet.
  - **Rio Grande Village Campground:** 1 ADA site, paved, flat, accessible restroom and water. Boardwalk trail nearby.
  - **Rio Grande Village RV Park:** Flat, paved, full hookups for RVs, accessible for mobility devices.
- **Park Entrances:** All main roads are paved and accessible by standard vehicles.

### Current Alerts (as of June 2025)
- Some road closures due to flooding (including paved road between Cottonwood Campground and Santa Elena Canyon, Hot Springs Rd, Old Maverick Rd, most dirt roads, and Boquillas Crossing).
- Chisos Basin improvement projects begin Fall 2025 (after your event).
- Panther Junction convenience store closed for remodel, but gas/diesel available.
- No drones allowed.
- Pets are restricted to developed areas and roads.

### Stargazing & Astronomy Events
- No astronomy events are currently scheduled for June 27–29, 2025. However, the park’s dark skies make it ideal for a DIY star party. Contact the park for possible ranger-led programs closer to your date.

### Campground Reservations
- All campgrounds require reservations: [Big Bend Campgrounds Info & Reservations](https://www.nps.gov/bibe/planyourvisit/camping.htm)

---

## 2. Padre Island National Seashore

**Why Padre Island?**
- Designated as an International Dark Sky Park.
- Offers beach stargazing and occasional astronomy programs (none currently scheduled for June 27–29, 2025).

### Accessibility

- **Visitor Center:** Malaquite Visitor Center is fully accessible, with accessible restrooms, ramp to the beach, and free beach wheelchair loan.
- **Campgrounds:**
  - **Malaquite Campground:** 2 accessible sites (#12, #13) near restrooms, showers, and accessible boardwalk to the beach. Paved and flat, but picnic tables are not wheelchair accessible.
  - **Bird Island Basin Campground:** Flat gravel, no designated accessible sites, but vault toilets are ramp-accessible.
- **Beach Access:** Accessible ramp from Malaquite Visitor Center to the beach; beach wheelchairs available.

### Current Alerts (as of June 2025)
- Canine distemper present—keep pets vaccinated or at home.
- Changing beach conditions—check tides and weather.
- Natural tar balls may be present on the beach.
- 4-wheel drive recommended for beach driving.

### Stargazing & Astronomy Events
- No astronomy events are currently scheduled for June 27–29, 2025. The beach is open for night sky viewing; check with the visitor center for possible last-minute programs.

### Campground Info
- All sites are first-come, first-served; arrive early for best selection.
- [Padre Island Camping Info](https://www.nps.gov/pais/planyourvisit/camping.htm)

---

## 3. Planning Tips for Accessibility

- Contact the visitor centers ahead of time for the most up-to-date accessibility information and to request accommodations.
- Bring red-light flashlights, accessible star charts, and plan for hot weather (hydration, sun protection).
- For group events, coordinate with park staff for accessible gathering locations and possible ranger support.
- For Big Bend, be aware of summer heat and limited shade; plan evening activities and bring cooling aids.

---

## 4. Contact Information

**Big Bend National Park**
- Website

name: Plan a National Park Eco-Friendly Backpacking and Sustainability Workshop in Washington for Summer 2025
description: Organize an eco-friendly backpacking trip in Washington state national parks during July 2025, focusing on sustainability education, zero-waste camping practices, and environmental stewardship. Identify suitable parks offering backpacking and educational activities, check for campgrounds and alerts, locate visitor centers for workshop sessions, and find events related to sustainability during the trip dates (2025-07-10 to 2025-07-13).
goal: To create an itinerary for an eco-conscious group backpacking adventure with sustainability workshops in Washington state national parks for July 10-13, 2025.

parkCode.description: Filter events by park code (e.g., "yose" for Yosemite). Multiple parks can be comma-separated (e.g., "yose,grca").

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return (default: 10, max: 50)

start.description: Start position for results (useful for pagination)

dateStart.description: Start date for filtering events (format: YYYY-MM-DD)

dateEnd.description: End date for filtering events (format: YYYY-MM-DD)

q.description: Search term to filter events by title or description

final_response:
Here’s a detailed plan for your National Park Eco-Friendly Backpacking and Sustainability Workshop in Washington, focusing on July 10–13, 2025. The itinerary is based on the best available options for backpacking, sustainability education, and group camping, with a focus on Mount Rainier National Park (the premier destination for backpacking and environmental stewardship in Washington).

---

## Recommended Park: Mount Rainier National Park

### Why Mount Rainier?
- Offers extensive backpacking and hiking trails (including the Wonderland Trail).
- Multiple campgrounds suitable for groups.
- Several visitor centers for educational workshops.
- Park staff and rangers often provide educational programming.
- Strong focus on wilderness preservation and Leave No Trace principles.

---

## Itinerary Outline

### Day 1: July 10, 2025 – Arrival & Orientation
- **Arrive at Cougar Rock Campground** (reservable, group sites available, ADA accessible).
    - Address: Mount Rainier National Park, Ashford, WA 98304
    - Reservations: [Recreation.gov - Cougar Rock](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232466)
- **Set up zero-waste base camp**: Demonstrate sustainable camping practices (waste sorting, reusable gear, food storage).
- **Evening orientation at the campground amphitheater**: Introduction to Leave No Trace, itinerary overview, and safety briefing.

### Day 2: July 11, 2025 – Backpacking & Sustainability Workshops
- **Morning**: Guided hike on the Wonderland Trail (access from Cougar Rock).
    - Focus: Trail stewardship, native flora/fauna, and minimal impact hiking.
- **Afternoon**: Workshop at the Henry M. Jackson Memorial Visitor Center (Paradise area).
    - Topics: Zero-waste backpacking, water purification, eco-friendly gear.
    - Facilities: Restrooms, exhibits, ranger-led programs.
- **Evening**: Group discussion and reflection at the campground.

### Day 3: July 12, 2025 – Environmental Stewardship in Action
- **Morning**: Volunteer activity or citizen science project (coordinate with park rangers).
    - Example: Trail maintenance, invasive species removal, or wildlife monitoring.
- **Afternoon**: Workshop at the Longmire Museum or Wilderness Information Center.
    - Topics: Climate change impacts on mountain ecosystems, sustainable travel.
- **Evening**: Campfire-free storytelling (fire ban in effect), stargazing, and eco-themed games.

### Day 4: July 13, 2025 – Wrap-up & Departure
- **Morning**: Final hike or group activity (e.g., wildflower identification, photography with a conservation focus).
- **Pack up camp**: Leave No Trace demonstration and group debrief.
- **Depart park by noon**.

---

## Key Logistics & Sustainability Notes

- **Campgrounds**: Cougar Rock is the best option (group sites, reservable, close to trails and visitor centers). White River Campground is first-come, first-served and also suitable, but less ideal for groups.
- **Fire Ban**: No campfires or open flames allowed in July 2025—plan for alternative cooking (stoves, cold meals).
- **Timed Entry**: If visiting the Sunrise area, a timed entry reservation is required July 11–Sept 1, 2025.
- **Delays**: Expect possible travel delays due to road work and busy summer visitation—plan accordingly.
- **Ohanapecosh Campground and Visitor Center**: Closed for construction in 2025.

---

## Educational Resources & Workshop Venues

- **Henry M. Jackson Memorial Visitor Center (Paradise)**: Open daily, exhibits, ranger programs, restrooms.
- **Longmire Museum & Wilderness Information Center**: Open daily, historic exhibits, ranger staff, maps, and educational materials.
- **Sunrise Visitor Center**: Open daily in July, exhibits, ranger staff (timed entry required for access).

---

## Sustainability & Zero-Waste Focus

- All meals should use reusable containers and utensils.
- Strict pack-in, pack-out policy for all waste.
- Workshops will include hands-on demonstrations of sustainable practices.
- Group will participate in stewardship or citizen science activity.

---

## No Scheduled Park Events on Sustainability (as of now)
- No specific sustainability events are listed for these dates, but ranger-led programs and citizen science opportunities are available—coordinate with park staff in advance.

---

## Alternative Park: Ebey’s Landing National Historical Reserve

- Offers state park campgrounds (Fort Casey, Fort Ebey), but less suited for backcountry backpacking and group sustainability workshops compared to Mount Rainier.
- Consider as a backup or for a more coastal, historical experience.

---

## Next Steps

1. Reserve group campsites at Cougar Rock as soon as possible.

Here’s a detailed plan for your National Park Eco-Friendly Backpacking and Sustainability Workshop in Washington, focusing on July 10–13, 2025. The itinerary is based on the best available options for backpacking, sustainability education, and group camping, with a focus on Mount Rainier National Park (the premier destination for backpacking and environmental stewardship in Washington).

---

## Recommended Park: Mount Rainier National Park

### Why Mount Rainier?
- Offers extensive backpacking and hiking trails (including the Wonderland Trail).
- Multiple campgrounds suitable for groups.
- Several visitor centers for educational workshops.
- Park staff and rangers often provide educational programming.
- Strong focus on wilderness preservation and Leave No Trace principles.

---

## Itinerary Outline

### Day 1: July 10, 2025 – Arrival & Orientation
- **Arrive at Cougar Rock Campground** (reservable, group sites available, ADA accessible).
    - Address: Mount Rainier National Park, Ashford, WA 98304
    - Reservations: [Recreation.gov - Cougar Rock](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232466)
- **Set up zero-waste base camp**: Demonstrate sustainable camping practices (waste sorting, reusable gear, food storage).
- **Evening orientation at the campground amphitheater**: Introduction to Leave No Trace, itinerary overview, and safety briefing.

### Day 2: July 11, 2025 – Backpacking & Sustainability Workshops
- **Morning**: Guided hike on the Wonderland Trail (access from Cougar Rock).
    - Focus: Trail stewardship, native flora/fauna, and minimal impact hiking.
- **Afternoon**: Workshop at the Henry M. Jackson Memorial Visitor Center (Paradise area).
    - Topics: Zero-waste backpacking, water purification, eco-friendly gear.
    - Facilities: Restrooms, exhibits, ranger-led programs.
- **Evening**: Group discussion and reflection at the campground.

### Day 3: July 12, 2025 – Environmental Stewardship in Action
- **Morning**: Volunteer activity or citizen science project (coordinate with park rangers).
    - Example: Trail maintenance, invasive species removal, or wildlife monitoring.
- **Afternoon**: Workshop at the Longmire Museum or Wilderness Information Center.
    - Topics: Climate change impacts on mountain ecosystems, sustainable travel.
- **Evening**: Campfire-free storytelling (fire ban in effect), stargazing, and eco-themed games.

### Day 4: July 13, 2025 – Wrap-up & Departure
- **Morning**: Final hike or group activity (e.g., wildflower identification, photography with a conservation focus).
- **Pack up camp**: Leave No Trace demonstration and group debrief.
- **Depart park by noon**.

---

## Key Logistics & Sustainability Notes

- **Campgrounds**: Cougar Rock is the best option (group sites, reservable, close to trails and visitor centers). White River Campground is first-come, first-served and also suitable, but less ideal for groups.
- **Fire Ban**: No campfires or open flames allowed in July 2025—plan for alternative cooking (stoves, cold meals).
- **Timed Entry**: If visiting the Sunrise area, a timed entry reservation is required July 11–Sept 1, 2025.
- **Delays**: Expect possible travel delays due to road work and busy summer visitation—plan accordingly.
- **Ohanapecosh Campground and Visitor Center**: Closed for construction in 2025.

---

## Educational Resources & Workshop Venues

- **Henry M. Jackson Memorial Visitor Center (Paradise)**: Open daily, exhibits, ranger programs, restrooms.
- **Longmire Museum & Wilderness Information Center**: Open daily, historic exhibits, ranger staff, maps, and educational materials.
- **Sunrise Visitor Center**: Open daily in July, exhibits, ranger staff (timed entry required for access).

---

## Sustainability & Zero-Waste Focus

- All meals should use reusable containers and utensils.
- Strict pack-in, pack-out policy for all waste.
- Workshops will include hands-on demonstrations of sustainable practices.
- Group will participate in stewardship or citizen science activity.

---

## No Scheduled Park Events on Sustainability (as of now)
- No specific sustainability events are listed for these dates, but ranger-led programs and citizen science opportunities are available—coordinate with park staff in advance.

---

## Alternative Park: Ebey’s Landing National Historical Reserve

- Offers state park campgrounds (Fort Casey, Fort Ebey), but less suited for backcountry backpacking and group sustainability workshops compared to Mount Rainier.
- Consider as a backup or for a more coastal, historical experience.

---

## Next Steps

1. Reserve group campsites at Cougar Rock as soon as possible.

final_response:
Here’s a romantic anniversary getaway plan for Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area in Georgia, a beautiful eastern US park known for its river, waterfalls, and lush scenery:

1. Park Overview:
- Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area offers scenic river views, hiking trails, and historic sites like the Marietta Paper Mill ruins (with waterfalls along Sope Creek).
- Location: 8800 Roberts Drive, Sandy Springs, GA 30350 (just north of Atlanta).
- Park website: https://www.nps.gov/chat/index.htm

2. Park Status & Alerts:
- The park is open and accessible during your dates (July 10–12, 2025).
- Paces Mill area will be open, but some land-based areas may have ongoing improvements. Most river and trail access will be available. See details: Paces Mill Renewal Project.

3. Camping:
- There are currently no official campgrounds within the park itself. However, there are many cozy campgrounds and romantic cabins nearby in the Atlanta/Sandy Springs area, or you can opt for a charming riverside Airbnb or bed & breakfast for a more intimate experience.

4. Special Events & Ranger-led Activities (July 10–12, 2025):
- July 11: Paddle the Park with Chattahoochee National Park Conservancy – A guided kayak/duckie trip on the river, perfect for couples seeking adventure and scenic views.
- July 12: Learn to Fish! – Join a ranger-led fishing basics class at Island Ford Pond. All gear provided; great for beginners and couples.
- July 12: Second Saturday Sweep – Join a friendly community cleanup hike along the river (Powers Island Unit), a unique way to connect with nature and each other.

5. Romantic Highlights:
- Hike to the Marietta Paper Mill ruins and Sope Creek waterfall for a picturesque picnic.
- Enjoy a sunset paddle or riverside stroll.
- Explore the park’s 66 miles of trails and 48 miles of riverbank, ideal for wildlife watching and photography.

6. Practical Info:
- Entrance fee: $5 per vehicle/day or $40 for an annual pass.
- Summer weather is warm and humid; pack light, breathable clothes, and bring water.
- Visitor Center: Island Ford Visitor Center, open 9am–5pm.

Here’s a romantic anniversary getaway plan for Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area in Georgia, a beautiful eastern US park known for its river, waterfalls, and lush scenery:

1. Park Overview:
- Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area offers scenic river views, hiking trails, and historic sites like the Marietta Paper Mill ruins (with waterfalls along Sope Creek).
- Location: 8800 Roberts Drive, Sandy Springs, GA 30350 (just north of Atlanta).
- Park website: https://www.nps.gov/chat/index.htm

2. Park Status & Alerts:
- The park is open and accessible during your dates (July 10–12, 2025).
- Paces Mill area will be open, but some land-based areas may have ongoing improvements. Most river and trail access will be available. See details: Paces Mill Renewal Project.

3. Camping:
- There are currently no official campgrounds within the park itself. However, there are many cozy campgrounds and romantic cabins nearby in the Atlanta/Sandy Springs area, or you can opt for a charming riverside Airbnb or bed & breakfast for a more intimate experience.

4. Special Events & Ranger-led Activities (July 10–12, 2025):
- July 11: Paddle the Park with Chattahoochee National Park Conservancy – A guided kayak/duckie trip on the river, perfect for couples seeking adventure and scenic views.
- July 12: Learn to Fish! – Join a ranger-led fishing basics class at Island Ford Pond. All gear provided; great for beginners and couples.
- July 12: Second Saturday Sweep – Join a friendly community cleanup hike along the river (Powers Island Unit), a unique way to connect with nature and each other.

5. Romantic Highlights:
- Hike to the Marietta Paper Mill ruins and Sope Creek waterfall for a picturesque picnic.
- Enjoy a sunset paddle or riverside stroll.
- Explore the park’s 66 miles of trails and 48 miles of riverbank, ideal for wildlife watching and photography.

6. Practical Info:
- Entrance fee: $5 per vehicle/day or $40 for an annual pass.
- Summer weather is warm and humid; pack light, breathable clothes, and bring water.
- Visitor Center: Island Ford Visitor Center, open 9am–5pm.

Would you like recommendations for nearby romantic accommodations or help booking event spots?

final_response:
Here is a comprehensive plan for your adventure race event in Rocky Mountain National Park (RMNP), including all the requested details:

1. Park Details & Available Activities
- Rocky Mountain National Park (RMNP) is located in Colorado and is renowned for its stunning mountain scenery, diverse wildlife, and a wide range of outdoor activities.
- Activities available: Hiking (extensive trail network), camping, ranger-led educational programs, wildlife viewing, fishing, birdwatching, and more.
- Weather in July: Expect mild to warm days (highs in the 70s-80s°F) and cool nights (40s-50s°F). Afternoon thunderstorms are common—plan accordingly.

2. Current Alerts or Closures
- Wild Basin Road Closure: From July 15–18, 2025, Wild Basin Road will be closed to all uses (vehicles, bikes, pedestrians) for maintenance. Sandbeach Lake Trailhead will remain accessible.
- Transponder Sales: Available at Beaver Meadows Visitor Center on Sundays (not directly related to your event, but useful for frequent park access).

3. Visitor Centers for Race Check-in
- Beaver Meadows Visitor Center (East side, near Estes Park): Open daily 9am–6pm in summer. Good for main check-in.
  Address: 1000 US Hwy 36, Estes Park, CO 80517
- Fall River Visitor Center (Near Fall River Entrance): Open daily 9am–5pm.
  Address: 3450 Fall River Road, Estes Park, CO 80517
- Kawuneeche Visitor Center (West side, near Grand Lake): Open daily 9am–5pm.
  Address: 16018 US Highway 34, Grand Lake, CO 80447
- Moraine Park Discovery Center (Bear Lake Road): Open daily 9am–4:30pm (mid-May to mid-October).
- Alpine Visitor Center (Trail Ridge Road, seasonal): Open daily 9:30am–5pm (summer only).
- Junior Ranger Headquarters at Hidden Valley: Open daily 9am–4:30pm (summer, for youth activities).
- Wilderness Office: For overnight backpacking permits, open daily 7am–3:30pm.

4. Available Campgrounds for Overnight Stays
- Aspenglen Campground: 52 sites, reservation only, near Fall River Entrance. Tents & RVs. $30/night. Reservations: recreation.gov (search "Aspenglen Campground").
- Glacier Basin Campground: 150+ sites, reservation only, near Bear Lake Road. Tents & RVs. $35/night (group sites available). Reservations: recreation.gov (search "Glacier Basin Campground").
- Longs Peak Campground: 26 tent-only sites, first-come, first-served, no water, vault toilets. $30/night.
- Moraine Park Campground: 244 sites, reservation only, reopening July 9–22, 2025 (your dates included). Tents & RVs, some electric hookups. $35–$55/night. Reservations: recreation.gov (search "Moraine Park Campground").
- Timber Creek Campground: 98 sites, reservation only, west side near Grand Lake. Tents & RVs. $35/night. Reservations: recreation.gov (search "Timber Creek Campground").

5. Park-Hosted Events (July 10–13, 2025)
You can incorporate these ranger-led and educational events into your itinerary:
- Discovering Rocky: Daily at Moraine Park Discovery Center—interactive ranger talks.
- High Country Tales: July 12 & 13 at Alpine Visitor Center—stories about humans and wildlife in the alpine world.
- Holzwarth Stories: July 10–13 at Holzwarth Historic Site—history of the Holzwarth family and early settlers.
- Critter Chat: July 10–13 at Kawuneeche Visitor Center—learn about local wildlife.
- Tundra Nature Walk: July 11 & 12 at Medicine Bow Curve Parking Area—guided walk in the alpine tundra.
- Junior Angler Adventures: July 10 at West Alluvial Fan Parking Area—fishing program for kids (permits required for ages 16+).
- Art Unleashed: Interactive Art Experience: July 12 at Fall River Visitor Center (details TBD).
- Discover Birding: July 12 at Upper Beaver Meadows Trailhead—guided bird walk.

Important Notes:
- Wild Basin Road closure may affect access to some southern trailheads July 15–18, but your event dates are just before this closure.
- All campgrounds (except Longs Peak) require advance reservations via recreation.gov.
- For group camping, Glacier Basin offers group sites.
- Weather can change rapidly; prepare for afternoon storms and cool nights.
- For more info or to coordinate special group activities

Here is a comprehensive plan for your adventure race event in Rocky Mountain National Park (RMNP), including all the requested details:

1. Park Details & Available Activities
- Rocky Mountain National Park (RMNP) is located in Colorado and is renowned for its stunning mountain scenery, diverse wildlife, and a wide range of outdoor activities.
- Activities available: Hiking (extensive trail network), camping, ranger-led educational programs, wildlife viewing, fishing, birdwatching, and more.
- Weather in July: Expect mild to warm days (highs in the 70s-80s°F) and cool nights (40s-50s°F). Afternoon thunderstorms are common—plan accordingly.

2. Current Alerts or Closures
- Wild Basin Road Closure: From July 15–18, 2025, Wild Basin Road will be closed to all uses (vehicles, bikes, pedestrians) for maintenance. Sandbeach Lake Trailhead will remain accessible.
- Transponder Sales: Available at Beaver Meadows Visitor Center on Sundays (not directly related to your event, but useful for frequent park access).

3. Visitor Centers for Race Check-in
- Beaver Meadows Visitor Center (East side, near Estes Park): Open daily 9am–6pm in summer. Good for main check-in.
  Address: 1000 US Hwy 36, Estes Park, CO 80517
- Fall River Visitor Center (Near Fall River Entrance): Open daily 9am–5pm.
  Address: 3450 Fall River Road, Estes Park, CO 80517
- Kawuneeche Visitor Center (West side, near Grand Lake): Open daily 9am–5pm.
  Address: 16018 US Highway 34, Grand Lake, CO 80447
- Moraine Park Discovery Center (Bear Lake Road): Open daily 9am–4:30pm (mid-May to mid-October).
- Alpine Visitor Center (Trail Ridge Road, seasonal): Open daily 9:30am–5pm (summer only).
- Junior Ranger Headquarters at Hidden Valley: Open daily 9am–4:30pm (summer, for youth activities).
- Wilderness Office: For overnight backpacking permits, open daily 7am–3:30pm.

4. Available Campgrounds for Overnight Stays
- Aspenglen Campground: 52 sites, reservation only, near Fall River Entrance. Tents & RVs. $30/night. Reservations: recreation.gov (search "Aspenglen Campground").
- Glacier Basin Campground: 150+ sites, reservation only, near Bear Lake Road. Tents & RVs. $35/night (group sites available). Reservations: recreation.gov (search "Glacier Basin Campground").
- Longs Peak Campground: 26 tent-only sites, first-come, first-served, no water, vault toilets. $30/night.
- Moraine Park Campground: 244 sites, reservation only, reopening July 9–22, 2025 (your dates included). Tents & RVs, some electric hookups. $35–$55/night. Reservations: recreation.gov (search "Moraine Park Campground").
- Timber Creek Campground: 98 sites, reservation only, west side near Grand Lake. Tents & RVs. $35/night. Reservations: recreation.gov (search "Timber Creek Campground").

5. Park-Hosted Events (July 10–13, 2025)
You can incorporate these ranger-led and educational events into your itinerary:
- Discovering Rocky: Daily at Moraine Park Discovery Center—interactive ranger talks.
- High Country Tales: July 12 & 13 at Alpine Visitor Center—stories about humans and wildlife in the alpine world.
- Holzwarth Stories: July 10–13 at Holzwarth Historic Site—history of the Holzwarth family and early settlers.
- Critter Chat: July 10–13 at Kawuneeche Visitor Center—learn about local wildlife.
- Tundra Nature Walk: July 11 & 12 at Medicine Bow Curve Parking Area—guided walk in the alpine tundra.
- Junior Angler Adventures: July 10 at West Alluvial Fan Parking Area—fishing program for kids (permits required for ages 16+).
- Art Unleashed: Interactive Art Experience: July 12 at Fall River Visitor Center (details TBD).
- Discover Birding: July 12 at Upper Beaver Meadows Trailhead—guided bird walk.

Important Notes:
- Wild Basin Road closure may affect access to some southern trailheads July 15–18, but your event dates are just before this closure.
- All campgrounds (except Longs Peak) require advance reservations via recreation.gov.
- For group camping, Glacier Basin offers group sites.
- Weather can change rapidly; prepare for afternoon storms and cool nights.
- For more info or to coordinate special group activities

final_response:
Here’s a detailed itinerary for a Louisiana National Park Culinary Heritage Tour for the week of October 13–19, 2025. This plan focuses on parks with strong food and cultural traditions, current alerts, educational visitor centers, and camping options (though no NPS campgrounds are available at these sites—see notes for alternatives).

---
## 1. Cane River Creole National Historical Park (Natchitoches, LA)
**Culinary & Cultural Focus:**  
- Explore Creole foodways, plantation kitchens, and the cultural history of enslaved and tenant workers.
- No food-specific events scheduled for your dates, but regular tours and exhibits highlight food traditions.

**Visitor Centers:**  
- Oakland Plantation Store (4386 Highway 494, Natchez, LA): Historic exhibits, open Wed–Sun, 9am–3:30pm.
- Magnolia Plantation Store (5549 Highway 119, Cloutierville, LA): Visitor contact station, open Wed–Sun, 9am–3:30pm.
- Texas & Pacific Railway Depot (1927 Remembrance Way, Natchitoches, LA): Exhibits on local history, open Wed–Sun, 9am–3:30pm.

**Current Alerts:**  
- Park hours: 9am–3:30pm, Wed–Sun.
- Oakland Main House interior open weekends only, 10am–2pm, self-guided tours.

**Camping:**  
- No NPS campgrounds. Consider local private or state park campgrounds (e.g., Kisatchie National Forest nearby).

---
## 2. Jean Lafitte National Historical Park and Preserve (Multiple Sites: New Orleans, Lafayette, Eunice, Marrero, Chalmette)
**Culinary & Cultural Focus:**  
- Deep dive into Cajun, Creole, and Acadian foodways.
- Prairie Acadian Cultural Center (Eunice, LA): Features cooking demonstrations, crafts, and music. Open Wed, Fri, Sat, 9:30am–4:30pm; Thu, 12–7pm; Tue, 9:30am–4:30pm.
- French Quarter Visitor Center (New Orleans): Exhibits on New Orleans’ food, music, and culture. Open Wed–Sat, 9:30am–4:30pm.
- Barataria Preserve (Marrero): Wetlands, trails, and exhibits on environmental influences on Louisiana cuisine.

**Current Alerts:**  
- Acadian Cultural Center (Lafayette) is temporarily closed due to air conditioning issues. Prairie Acadian Cultural Center in Eunice is open and hosting programs.

**Visitor Centers:**  
- Prairie Acadian Cultural Center (250 Park Ave, Eunice, LA)
- French Quarter Visitor Center (419 Decatur St, New Orleans, LA)
- Barataria Preserve (6588 Barataria Blvd, Marrero, LA)
- Chalmette Battlefield (1 Battlefield Rd, Chalmette, LA)

**Camping:**  
- No NPS campgrounds. Look for nearby state parks or private campgrounds (e.g., Bayou Segnette State Park near Barataria).

---
## 3. Poverty Point National Monument (Northeastern LA)
**Culinary & Cultural Focus:**  
- Learn about ancient foodways and trade networks of the Poverty Point culture.
- No food-specific events scheduled, but the visitor center has exhibits on prehistoric diets and food gathering.

**Visitor Center:**  
- Poverty Point World Heritage Site (managed by Louisiana State Parks): Open daily, 9am–5pm.

**Current Alerts:**  
- Park and visitor center open; call ahead for latest info and COVID-19 precautions.

**Camping:**  
- No NPS campgrounds, but Poverty Point Reservoir State Park nearby offers camping.

Here is a comprehensive plan for your family reunion at a national park in Ohio, focusing on accessibility, safety, and logistics:

## Recommended Park: Cuyahoga Valley National Park

### Why Cuyahoga Valley?
- **Accessible Activities:** Offers a wide range of accessible activities for all ages and abilities, including biking, hiking, scenic train rides, picnicking, paddling, and Junior Ranger programs.
- **Family-Friendly:** The park is large, scenic, and close to both Cleveland and Akron, making it convenient for travel and accommodations.

---

## Safety & Alerts (as of April 2025)
- **Restroom Closures:** Some restrooms are closed until further notice. Check the latest updates before your visit: [Park Conditions](https://www.nps.gov/cuva/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
- **Crowding:** Expect crowded parking lots and popular spots, especially on weekends and warm days between 10 am and 3 pm.
- **Trail Status:** East Rim trails may close in wet or hazardous conditions. Check real-time status: [East Rim Trail Updates](https://twitter.com/cvnpmtb)
- **Theft Warning:** Car break-ins have increased. Do not leave valuables in your car; lock items in your trunk before arriving. More info: [Safety Tips](https://www.nps.gov/cuva/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
- **Area Closures:** The former golf course property (including part of the Valley Trail) is closed for environmental remediation.

---

## Visitor Centers (for Planning & Accessibility)
1. **Boston Mill Visitor Center**
   - Address: 6947 Riverview Road, Peninsula, OH 44264
   - Hours: Daily, 9:30 am – 5:00 pm (March–December)
   - Features: Trip planning, park info, accessible restrooms (open even when the center is closed)
   - Directions: [Boston Mill Directions](https://www.nps.gov/cuva/planyourvisit/directions.htm)
   - Phone: 440-717-3890

2. **Canal Exploration Center**
   - Address: 7104 Canal Road, Valley View, OH 44125
   - Hours: Thurs–Sun, 10:00 am – 4:00 pm (summer season)
   - Features: Interactive exhibits, accessible restrooms at trailhead

3. **Hunt House**
   - Address: 2054 Bolanz Road, Peninsula, OH 44264
   - Features: Child-friendly nature exhibits, rest area, open seasonally

---

## Campgrounds
- **No NPS-operated campgrounds** are currently available within Cuyahoga Valley National Park. You may need to look for nearby private or state park campgrounds for overnight stays.

---

## Accessibility & Activities
- **Accessible Trails:** The Towpath Trail and several boardwalks are wheelchair accessible.
- **Scenic Train:** The Cuyahoga Valley Scenic Railroad offers accessible cars.
- **Picnic Areas:** Multiple accessible picnic spots throughout the park.
- **Visitor Centers:** All main visitor centers are accessible and have accessible restrooms.
- **Programs:** Junior Ranger and interpretive programs are available for all ages.

---

## Planning Tips
- Arrive early to secure parking, especially if visiting on a weekend.
- Contact the visitor center for the latest accessibility details and restroom availability.
- Consider booking nearby hotels or private campgrounds for overnight accommodations.
- Remind guests about vehicle safety and not to leave valuables in cars.

---

### Useful Links
- [Cuyahoga Valley National Park Official Site](https://www.nps.gov/cuva/index.htm)
- [Accessibility at CVNP](https://www.nps.gov/cuva/planyourvisit/accessibility.htm)
- [Park Map & Directions](https://www.nps.gov/cuva/planyourvisit/maps.htm)

Would you like recommendations for nearby campgrounds or accessible lodging options outside the park? Or do you need help with activity ideas and group logistics?

Here is a comprehensive plan for your family reunion at a national park in Ohio, focusing on accessibility, safety, and logistics:

## Recommended Park: Cuyahoga Valley National Park

### Why Cuyahoga Valley?
- **Accessible Activities:** Offers a wide range of accessible activities for all ages and abilities, including biking, hiking, scenic train rides, picnicking, paddling, and Junior Ranger programs.
- **Family-Friendly:** The park is large, scenic, and close to both Cleveland and Akron, making it convenient for travel and accommodations.

---

## Safety & Alerts (as of April 2025)
- **Restroom Closures:** Some restrooms are closed until further notice. Check the latest updates before your visit: [Park Conditions](https://www.nps.gov/cuva/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
- **Crowding:** Expect crowded parking lots and popular spots, especially on weekends and warm days between 10 am and 3 pm.
- **Trail Status:** East Rim trails may close in wet or hazardous conditions. Check real-time status: [East Rim Trail Updates](https://twitter.com/cvnpmtb)
- **Theft Warning:** Car break-ins have increased. Do not leave valuables in your car; lock items in your trunk before arriving. More info: [Safety Tips](https://www.nps.gov/cuva/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
- **Area Closures:** The former golf course property (including part of the Valley Trail) is closed for environmental remediation.

---

## Visitor Centers (for Planning & Accessibility)
1. **Boston Mill Visitor Center**
   - Address: 6947 Riverview Road, Peninsula, OH 44264
   - Hours: Daily, 9:30 am – 5:00 pm (March–December)
   - Features: Trip planning, park info, accessible restrooms (open even when the center is closed)
   - Directions: [Boston Mill Directions](https://www.nps.gov/cuva/planyourvisit/directions.htm)
   - Phone: 440-717-3890

2. **Canal Exploration Center**
   - Address: 7104 Canal Road, Valley View, OH 44125
   - Hours: Thurs–Sun, 10:00 am – 4:00 pm (summer season)
   - Features: Interactive exhibits, accessible restrooms at trailhead

3. **Hunt House**
   - Address: 2054 Bolanz Road, Peninsula, OH 44264
   - Features: Child-friendly nature exhibits, rest area, open seasonally

---

## Campgrounds
- **No NPS-operated campgrounds** are currently available within Cuyahoga Valley National Park. You may need to look for nearby private or state park campgrounds for overnight stays.

---

## Accessibility & Activities
- **Accessible Trails:** The Towpath Trail and several boardwalks are wheelchair accessible.
- **Scenic Train:** The Cuyahoga Valley Scenic Railroad offers accessible cars.
- **Picnic Areas:** Multiple accessible picnic spots throughout the park.
- **Visitor Centers:** All main visitor centers are accessible and have accessible restrooms.
- **Programs:** Junior Ranger and interpretive programs are available for all ages.

---

## Planning Tips
- Arrive early to secure parking, especially if visiting on a weekend.
- Contact the visitor center for the latest accessibility details and restroom availability.
- Consider booking nearby hotels or private campgrounds for overnight accommodations.
- Remind guests about vehicle safety and not to leave valuables in cars.

---

### Useful Links
- [Cuyahoga Valley National Park Official Site](https://www.nps.gov/cuva/index.htm)
- [Accessibility at CVNP](https://www.nps.gov/cuva/planyourvisit/accessibility.htm)
- [Park Map & Directions](https://www.nps.gov/cuva/planyourvisit/maps.htm)

final_response:
Here is a comprehensive trip plan for an Accessible Wildlife and Nature Education Weekend in South Carolina National Parks for June 14–15, 2025. This plan focuses on parks with accessible wildlife viewing, nature education programs, and facilities that support students with accessibility needs.

---
## Recommended Parks & Key Details

### 1. Congaree National Park
- **Location:** 100 National Park Road, Hopkins, SC 29061
- **Description:** Home to the largest intact old-growth bottomland hardwood forest in the Southeast, with rich biodiversity and accessible boardwalks for wildlife viewing.
- **Accessibility:** The Harry Hampton Visitor Center and boardwalk trail are accessible. The Longleaf Campground offers a designated accessible campsite.
- **Wildlife/Nature Education:** Guided walks, ranger talks, and Junior Ranger programs.
- **Website:** [Congaree National Park](https://www.nps.gov/cong/index.htm)

### 2. Charles Pinckney National Historic Site
- **Location:** 1254 Long Point Road, Mount Pleasant, SC 29464
- **Description:** Preserves Snee Farm, with accessible grounds, a historic house visitor center, and interpretive exhibits on local history and nature.
- **Accessibility:** Visitor center and grounds are generally accessible.
- **Wildlife/Nature Education:** Self-guided nature walks, museum exhibits, and Junior Ranger program.
- **Website:** [Charles Pinckney NHS](https://www.nps.gov/chpi/index.htm)

### 3. Fort Sumter and Fort Moultrie National Historical Park
- **Locations:** 
  - Fort Moultrie: 1214 Middle Street, Sullivan’s Island, SC 29482
  - Fort Sumter Visitor Center: 340 Concord Street, Charleston, SC 29401
- **Description:** Historic forts with museum exhibits, wildlife viewing (especially birds), and ranger-led programs.
- **Accessibility:** Fort Moultrie Visitor Center is accessible. Note: Ferries from Patriots Point to Fort Sumter are NOT wheelchair accessible; use Liberty Square departure.
- **Website:** [Fort Sumter & Fort Moultrie NHP](https://www.nps.gov/fosu/index.htm)

### 4. Ninety Six National Historic Site
- **Location:** 1103 Hwy 248 S, Ninety Six, SC 29666
- **Description:** Revolutionary War site with accessible visitor center, museum, and trails for wildlife and history exploration.
- **Accessibility:** Visitor center and some trails are accessible.
- **Wildlife/Nature Education:** Guided tours, museum exhibits, and Junior Ranger program.
- **Website:** [Ninety Six NHS](https://www.nps.gov/nisi/index.htm)

---
## Alerts & Closures (as of June 2025)

- **Congaree NP:** Lower section of the boardwalk loop is closed for construction, but the Weston Lake Overlook is open. [Details & Map](https://www.nps.gov/cong/boardwalk-construction-updates.htm)
- **Fort Sumter/Fort Moultrie NHP:** 
  - Ferries from Patriots Point are not wheelchair accessible; use Liberty Square for accessible ferry boarding.
  - Fort Moultrie Fishing Dock and Main Picnic Area are closed until Spring 2026; alternate picnic area available.
- **Ninety Six NHS:** Some trails and an equestrian bridge are closed; most trails and the visitor center are open. Exercise caution due to possible storm debris.
- **General:** Always check park websites for the latest updates before visiting.

---
## Visitor Centers with Accessible Facilities

- **Congaree NP:** Harry Hampton Visitor Center (open daily 9am–5pm, accessible restrooms, exhibits, bookstore)
- **Charles Pinckney NHS:** Historic house visitor center (open Fri–Sun 9am–4:30pm, accessible)
- **Fort Moultrie Visitor Center:** Accessible, open daily 9am–4:30pm
- **Fort Sumter Visitor Center at Liberty Square:** Accessible, open daily 8:30am–4:30pm
- **Ninety Six NHS Visitor Center:** Open Wed–Sun 9am–4:30pm, accessible

---
## Accessible Campgrounds

**Congaree National Park:**
- **Longleaf Campground:** 
  - Group and individual tent sites, vault toilets, water at visitor center.
  - Campsite #1 is designated for accessibility needs (flat dirt path, some trip hazards).
  - [Reserve here](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/10190876)
- **Bluff Campground:** 
  - Hike-in, rustic, not recommended for standard wheelchairs.

*No campgrounds at Charles Pinckney, Fort Sumter/Moultrie, or Ninety Six

Here is a comprehensive trip plan for an Accessible Wildlife and Nature Education Weekend in South Carolina National Parks for June 14–15, 2025. This plan focuses on parks with accessible wildlife viewing, nature education programs, and facilities that support students with accessibility needs.

---
## Recommended Parks & Key Details

### 1. Congaree National Park
- **Location:** 100 National Park Road, Hopkins, SC 29061
- **Description:** Home to the largest intact old-growth bottomland hardwood forest in the Southeast, with rich biodiversity and accessible boardwalks for wildlife viewing.
- **Accessibility:** The Harry Hampton Visitor Center and boardwalk trail are accessible. The Longleaf Campground offers a designated accessible campsite.
- **Wildlife/Nature Education:** Guided walks, ranger talks, and Junior Ranger programs.
- **Website:** [Congaree National Park](https://www.nps.gov/cong/index.htm)

### 2. Charles Pinckney National Historic Site
- **Location:** 1254 Long Point Road, Mount Pleasant, SC 29464
- **Description:** Preserves Snee Farm, with accessible grounds, a historic house visitor center, and interpretive exhibits on local history and nature.
- **Accessibility:** Visitor center and grounds are generally accessible.
- **Wildlife/Nature Education:** Self-guided nature walks, museum exhibits, and Junior Ranger program.
- **Website:** [Charles Pinckney NHS](https://www.nps.gov/chpi/index.htm)

### 3. Fort Sumter and Fort Moultrie National Historical Park
- **Locations:** 
  - Fort Moultrie: 1214 Middle Street, Sullivan’s Island, SC 29482
  - Fort Sumter Visitor Center: 340 Concord Street, Charleston, SC 29401
- **Description:** Historic forts with museum exhibits, wildlife viewing (especially birds), and ranger-led programs.
- **Accessibility:** Fort Moultrie Visitor Center is accessible. Note: Ferries from Patriots Point to Fort Sumter are NOT wheelchair accessible; use Liberty Square departure.
- **Website:** [Fort Sumter & Fort Moultrie NHP](https://www.nps.gov/fosu/index.htm)

### 4. Ninety Six National Historic Site
- **Location:** 1103 Hwy 248 S, Ninety Six, SC 29666
- **Description:** Revolutionary War site with accessible visitor center, museum, and trails for wildlife and history exploration.
- **Accessibility:** Visitor center and some trails are accessible.
- **Wildlife/Nature Education:** Guided tours, museum exhibits, and Junior Ranger program.
- **Website:** [Ninety Six NHS](https://www.nps.gov/nisi/index.htm)

---
## Alerts & Closures (as of June 2025)

- **Congaree NP:** Lower section of the boardwalk loop is closed for construction, but the Weston Lake Overlook is open. [Details & Map](https://www.nps.gov/cong/boardwalk-construction-updates.htm)
- **Fort Sumter/Fort Moultrie NHP:** 
  - Ferries from Patriots Point are not wheelchair accessible; use Liberty Square for accessible ferry boarding.
  - Fort Moultrie Fishing Dock and Main Picnic Area are closed until Spring 2026; alternate picnic area available.
- **Ninety Six NHS:** Some trails and an equestrian bridge are closed; most trails and the visitor center are open. Exercise caution due to possible storm debris.
- **General:** Always check park websites for the latest updates before visiting.

---
## Visitor Centers with Accessible Facilities

- **Congaree NP:** Harry Hampton Visitor Center (open daily 9am–5pm, accessible restrooms, exhibits, bookstore)
- **Charles Pinckney NHS:** Historic house visitor center (open Fri–Sun 9am–4:30pm, accessible)
- **Fort Moultrie Visitor Center:** Accessible, open daily 9am–4:30pm
- **Fort Sumter Visitor Center at Liberty Square:** Accessible, open daily 8:30am–4:30pm
- **Ninety Six NHS Visitor Center:** Open Wed–Sun 9am–4:30pm, accessible

---
## Accessible Campgrounds

**Congaree National Park:**
- **Longleaf Campground:** 
  - Group and individual tent sites, vault toilets, water at visitor center.
  - Campsite #1 is designated for accessibility needs (flat dirt path, some trip hazards).

final_response:
Here’s a detailed itinerary and planning guide for a National Park Kayaking and Ranger Program Weekend in Minnesota for July 12-13, 2025. This plan focuses on parks with kayaking and ranger-led programs, with all the details you need for a fun and educational adventure!

---
## Top National Parks in Minnesota for Kayaking & Ranger Programs

### 1. Mississippi National River & Recreation Area (MISS)
- **Location:** St. Paul, MN
- **Activities:** Kayaking, canoeing, ranger-led wildlife programs, hiking, birdwatching.
- **Ranger-Led Events:**
  - **Paddle with a Ranger: Vermillion River Bottoms**
    - Dates: July 12 & 13, 2025
    - Description: Guided paddle through the Vermillion River floodplain forest. Great for wildlife viewing (bald eagles, herons, etc.). For intermediate/advanced paddlers (not for first-timers). Equipment provided. Registration required.
    - Location: Vermillion River North Public Water Access, 17208 Ravenna Trail, Hastings, MN 55033
  - **Discovery Table**
    - Dates: July 12 & 13, 2025 (and most summer weekends)
    - Description: Drop-in ranger table at the Mississippi River Visitor Center with wildlife, history, and nature topics. Great for families and kids.
- **Visitor Center:** Mississippi River Visitor Center, 120 Kellogg Blvd West, St. Paul, MN 55102. Open 9am–5pm (closed Mondays).
- **Alerts:** Visitor Center will be open during your weekend.
- **Camping:** No NPS campgrounds, but private and state park campgrounds are nearby.

### 2. Saint Croix National Scenic Riverway (SACN)
- **Location:** Eastern MN/WI border
- **Activities:** Kayaking, canoeing, camping, wildlife watching, ranger programs.
- **Visitor Centers:**
  - St. Croix River Visitor Center (St. Croix Falls, WI) – Open daily 10am–5pm.
  - Namekagon River Visitor Center (Trego, WI) – Open Thurs–Mon, 10am–5pm.
- **Camping:** 
  - Primitive, first-come, first-served campsites along the river (Middle St. Croix, Lower St. Croix, Namekagon Districts). Free, but some require a permit.
  - No reservations; arrive early for best selection.
- **Alerts:** Increased bear activity along the Namekagon River—store food properly!
- **Ranger-Led Events:** None listed for this weekend, but check at the visitor center for possible pop-up programs.

### 3. Voyageurs National Park (VOYA)
- **Location:** Northern MN, near International Falls
- **Activities:** Kayaking, canoeing, camping, hiking, wildlife watching, ranger programs.
- **Visitor Centers:**
  - Rainy Lake, Kabetogama Lake, Ash River, Crane Lake (all open 9am–5pm in summer).
- **Camping:** Multiple water-accessible campsites (reservations recommended).
- **Ranger-Led Events:** None listed for this weekend, but check with visitor centers for updated schedules.
- **Note:** This park is best for groups with their own boats or who can rent locally.

### 4. Grand Portage National Monument (GRPO)
- **Location:** NE tip of MN, on Lake Superior
- **Activities:** Canoe/kayak camping, hiking, cultural programs, wildlife watching.
- **Visitor Center:** Heritage Center, 170 Mile Creek Road, Grand Portage, MN 55605 (open 9am–5pm).
- **Camping:** Fort Charlotte Backcountry Campgrounds (canoe/hike-in, permit required, free).
- **Ranger-Led Events:** Check with the Heritage Center for cultural and wildlife programs.

---
## Sample Itinerary: Mississippi National River & Recreation Area

### Friday, July 11
- Arrive in the Twin Cities area. Set up camp at a nearby state park or private campground.

### Saturday, July 12
- Morning: Visit the Mississippi River Visitor Center (9am–5pm) for orientation and Discovery Table.
- Midday: Lunch in St. Paul or picnic by the river.
- Afternoon: Join “Paddle with a Ranger: Vermillion River Bottoms” (register in advance; all equipment provided).
- Evening: Camp at a nearby campground.

### Sunday, July 13
- Morning: Optional second “Paddle with a Ranger” or Discovery Table at the Visitor Center.
- Afternoon: Explore hiking/biking trails or visit another park (Saint Croix Riverway or Grand Portage if you want to extend your trip).
- Depart for home.

Here’s a detailed itinerary and planning guide for a National Park Kayaking and Ranger Program Weekend in Minnesota for July 12-13, 2025. This plan focuses on parks with kayaking and ranger-led programs, with all the details you need for a fun and educational adventure!

---
## Top National Parks in Minnesota for Kayaking & Ranger Programs

### 1. Mississippi National River & Recreation Area (MISS)
- **Location:** St. Paul, MN
- **Activities:** Kayaking, canoeing, ranger-led wildlife programs, hiking, birdwatching.
- **Ranger-Led Events:**
  - **Paddle with a Ranger: Vermillion River Bottoms**
    - Dates: July 12 & 13, 2025
    - Description: Guided paddle through the Vermillion River floodplain forest. Great for wildlife viewing (bald eagles, herons, etc.). For intermediate/advanced paddlers (not for first-timers). Equipment provided. Registration required.
    - Location: Vermillion River North Public Water Access, 17208 Ravenna Trail, Hastings, MN 55033
  - **Discovery Table**
    - Dates: July 12 & 13, 2025 (and most summer weekends)
    - Description: Drop-in ranger table at the Mississippi River Visitor Center with wildlife, history, and nature topics. Great for families and kids.
- **Visitor Center:** Mississippi River Visitor Center, 120 Kellogg Blvd West, St. Paul, MN 55102. Open 9am–5pm (closed Mondays).
- **Alerts:** Visitor Center will be open during your weekend.
- **Camping:** No NPS campgrounds, but private and state park campgrounds are nearby.

### 2. Saint Croix National Scenic Riverway (SACN)
- **Location:** Eastern MN/WI border
- **Activities:** Kayaking, canoeing, camping, wildlife watching, ranger programs.
- **Visitor Centers:**
  - St. Croix River Visitor Center (St. Croix Falls, WI) – Open daily 10am–5pm.
  - Namekagon River Visitor Center (Trego, WI) – Open Thurs–Mon, 10am–5pm.
- **Camping:** 
  - Primitive, first-come, first-served campsites along the river (Middle St. Croix, Lower St. Croix, Namekagon Districts). Free, but some require a permit.
  - No reservations; arrive early for best selection.
- **Alerts:** Increased bear activity along the Namekagon River—store food properly!
- **Ranger-Led Events:** None listed for this weekend, but check at the visitor center for possible pop-up programs.

### 3. Voyageurs National Park (VOYA)
- **Location:** Northern MN, near International Falls
- **Activities:** Kayaking, canoeing, camping, hiking, wildlife watching, ranger programs.
- **Visitor Centers:**
  - Rainy Lake, Kabetogama Lake, Ash River, Crane Lake (all open 9am–5pm in summer).
- **Camping:** Multiple water-accessible campsites (reservations recommended).
- **Ranger-Led Events:** None listed for this weekend, but check with visitor centers for updated schedules.
- **Note:** This park is best for groups with their own boats or who can rent locally.

### 4. Grand Portage National Monument (GRPO)
- **Location:** NE tip of MN, on Lake Superior
- **Activities:** Canoe/kayak camping, hiking, cultural programs, wildlife watching.
- **Visitor Center:** Heritage Center, 170 Mile Creek Road, Grand Portage, MN 55605 (open 9am–5pm).
- **Camping:** Fort Charlotte Backcountry Campgrounds (canoe/hike-in, permit required, free).
- **Ranger-Led Events:** Check with the Heritage Center for cultural and wildlife programs.

---
## Sample Itinerary: Mississippi National River & Recreation Area

### Friday, July 11
- Arrive in the Twin Cities area. Set up camp at a nearby state park or private campground.

### Saturday, July 12
- Morning: Visit the Mississippi River Visitor Center (9am–5pm) for orientation and Discovery Table.
- Midday: Lunch in St. Paul or picnic by the river.
- Afternoon: Join “Paddle with a Ranger: Vermillion River Bottoms” (register in advance; all equipment provided).
- Evening: Camp at a nearby campground.

### Sunday, July 13
- Morning: Optional second “Paddle with a Ranger” or Discovery Table at the Visitor Center.
- Afternoon: Explore hiking/biking trails or visit another park (Saint Croix Riverway or Grand Portage if you want to extend your trip).
- Depart for home.

final_response:
Here is a comprehensive plan for a family-friendly Astronomy and Camping Weekend at Craters of the Moon National Monument & Preserve in Idaho, for July 12-13, 2025:

Park Selection & Overview
- Chosen Park: Craters of the Moon National Monument & Preserve (ID)
- Why: Designated an International Dark Sky Park, Craters of the Moon is one of the best places in the country for stargazing. It offers family-friendly camping, ranger programs, hiking, and unique volcanic landscapes.
- Park Website: https://www.nps.gov/crmo/index.htm

Safety & Current Alerts
- Visitor Center Voicemail Down: The visitor center can make and receive calls, but voicemail is not working. Call 208-527-1335 between 8 am–6 pm MT or email crmo_information@nps.gov for assistance.
- Navigation Alert: Do not rely on GPS. The visitor center is at 1266 Craters Loop Road, Arco, ID, just off US Hwy 20/26/93. Directions: https://www.nps.gov/crmo/planyourvisit/directions.htm

Visitor Services
- Robert Limbert Visitor Center
  - Address: 1266 Craters Loop Road, Arco, ID 83213
  - Hours (mid-summer): 8:30 am–6 pm, 7 days/week
  - Services: Maps, bookstore, passport stamps, restrooms, information
  - Directions: See above or park website
  - Phone: 208-527-1335

Camping Options
- Lava Flow Campground
  - 42 sites, first-come, first-served (no reservations)
  - Open to vehicles May–November (weather dependent)
  - Fees: $15/night (regular), $7.50 with Senior/Access Pass
  - Amenities: Flush/vault toilets, potable water (seasonal), dump station, amphitheater, recycling, camp store, food storage lockers, ice/firewood for sale, cell reception, ADA accessible restrooms and site
  - No wood fires; quiet hours 10 pm–6 am; no RV hookups
  - Suitable for tents and RVs (no max length specified)
  - More info: https://www.nps.gov/crmo/planyourvisit/camping.htm

Astronomy & Family Activities
- Stargazing: Craters of the Moon is renowned for its dark skies and is ideal for family stargazing. Bring your own telescope or binoculars for the best experience.
- Junior Ranger Program: Available at the visitor center for kids.
- Hiking: Family-friendly trails explore volcanic features, cinder cones, and lava tubes.
- No astronomy-specific events are scheduled for July 12-13, 2025, but the park’s dark sky status makes it perfect for your own night sky activities.

Entrance Fees
- $20 per private vehicle (covers all passengers for 7 days)
- $10 per person (walk-in/bike), free for youth 15 and under
- Annual park pass: $35

Weather
- July weather: Hot days (highs in 90s°F), cool nights, strong sun, and possible afternoon winds. Bring sun protection, layers, and plenty of water.

Summary for Families
- Craters of the Moon offers a safe, accessible, and unique setting for a family astronomy and camping weekend.
- The Lava Flow Campground is family-friendly with essential amenities.
- The park’s International Dark Sky status ensures excellent stargazing.
- The visitor center provides educational resources and ranger programs for kids.
- No scheduled astronomy events that weekend, but the setting is ideal for your own stargazing activities.

Tips
- Arrive early for a campsite (first-come, first-served).
- Bring red flashlights for night sky viewing.
- Prepare for hot days and cool nights.
- Check the park website for last-minute alerts or updates.

Enjoy your family astronomy and camping adventure at Craters of the Moon!

Here is a comprehensive plan for a family-friendly Astronomy and Camping Weekend at Craters of the Moon National Monument & Preserve in Idaho, for July 12-13, 2025:

Park Selection & Overview
- Chosen Park: Craters of the Moon National Monument & Preserve (ID)
- Why: Designated an International Dark Sky Park, Craters of the Moon is one of the best places in the country for stargazing. It offers family-friendly camping, ranger programs, hiking, and unique volcanic landscapes.
- Park Website: https://www.nps.gov/crmo/index.htm

Safety & Current Alerts
- Visitor Center Voicemail Down: The visitor center can make and receive calls, but voicemail is not working. Call 208-527-1335 between 8 am–6 pm MT or email crmo_information@nps.gov for assistance.
- Navigation Alert: Do not rely on GPS. The visitor center is at 1266 Craters Loop Road, Arco, ID, just off US Hwy 20/26/93. Directions: https://www.nps.gov/crmo/planyourvisit/directions.htm

Visitor Services
- Robert Limbert Visitor Center
  - Address: 1266 Craters Loop Road, Arco, ID 83213
  - Hours (mid-summer): 8:30 am–6 pm, 7 days/week
  - Services: Maps, bookstore, passport stamps, restrooms, information
  - Directions: See above or park website
  - Phone: 208-527-1335

Camping Options
- Lava Flow Campground
  - 42 sites, first-come, first-served (no reservations)
  - Open to vehicles May–November (weather dependent)
  - Fees: $15/night (regular), $7.50 with Senior/Access Pass
  - Amenities: Flush/vault toilets, potable water (seasonal), dump station, amphitheater, recycling, camp store, food storage lockers, ice/firewood for sale, cell reception, ADA accessible restrooms and site
  - No wood fires; quiet hours 10 pm–6 am; no RV hookups
  - Suitable for tents and RVs (no max length specified)
  - More info: https://www.nps.gov/crmo/planyourvisit/camping.htm

Astronomy & Family Activities
- Stargazing: Craters of the Moon is renowned for its dark skies and is ideal for family stargazing. Bring your own telescope or binoculars for the best experience.
- Junior Ranger Program: Available at the visitor center for kids.
- Hiking: Family-friendly trails explore volcanic features, cinder cones, and lava tubes.
- No astronomy-specific events are scheduled for July 12-13, 2025, but the park’s dark sky status makes it perfect for your own night sky activities.

Entrance Fees
- $20 per private vehicle (covers all passengers for 7 days)
- $10 per person (walk-in/bike), free for youth 15 and under
- Annual park pass: $35

Weather
- July weather: Hot days (highs in 90s°F), cool nights, strong sun, and possible afternoon winds. Bring sun protection, layers, and plenty of water.

Summary for Families
- Craters of the Moon offers a safe, accessible, and unique setting for a family astronomy and camping weekend.
- The Lava Flow Campground is family-friendly with essential amenities.
- The park’s International Dark Sky status ensures excellent stargazing.
- The visitor center provides educational resources and ranger programs for kids.
- No scheduled astronomy events that weekend, but the setting is ideal for your own stargazing activities.

Tips
- Arrive early for a campsite (first-come, first-served).
- Bring red flashlights for night sky viewing.
- Prepare for hot days and cool nights.
- Check the park website for last-minute alerts or updates.

Enjoy your family astronomy and camping adventure at Craters of the Moon!

final_response:
Here is a comprehensive, accessible history and culture tour itinerary for Massachusetts national parks, tailored for visitors with mobility needs. This plan includes park highlights, accessibility notes, current alerts, visitor centers, and overnight stay options.

---
## 1. Adams National Historical Park (Quincy, MA)
- **Highlights:** Historic homes of John and John Quincy Adams, Peace field estate, Stone Library, gardens.
- **Accessibility:** The Visitor Center is accessible and offers an introductory film. Some historic homes may have limited accessibility; call ahead for details.
- **Current Alerts:**
  - July 11–12: Visitor Center closed; operations moved to Peace field Carriage House. Park closes at 1pm on July 12.
  - Heat Notice: Tours may be modified/cancelled due to high temperatures. Call ahead for updates.
- **Visitor Center:** 1250 Hancock Street, Quincy, MA. Open Wed–Sun, 9am–5pm. Free validated parking available.
- **Contact:** 617-770-1175 | adam_visitor_center@nps.gov

---
## 2. Blackstone River Valley National Historical Park (MA/RI border)
- **Highlights:** Slater Mill (birthplace of American industry), canal, historic mill villages.
- **Accessibility:** Visitor Center at Old Slater Mill is seasonally open (Thurs–Sun, 10am–4pm). Grounds are open dawn to dusk. Contact for accessibility details.
- **Current Alerts:** July 10 Walkabout cancelled (inclement weather); resumes July 17.
- **Visitor Center:** 67 Roosevelt Avenue, Pawtucket, RI.
- **Contact:** 401-725-8638 | blrv_info@nps.gov

---
## 3. Boston African American National Historic Site (Boston, MA)
- **Highlights:** Black Heritage Trail, Museum of African American History, historic homes and meeting houses.
- **Accessibility:** Faneuil Hall Visitor Center is accessible and offers maps, information, and accessible restrooms. Some trail sites may have uneven terrain; check with rangers for accessible routes.
- **Visitor Center:** Faneuil Hall, Dock Square, Boston, MA. Open daily 10am–5pm.
- **Contact:** 617-429-6760 | boaf_mail@nps.gov

---
## 4. Boston National Historical Park (Boston, MA)
- **Highlights:** Freedom Trail, Bunker Hill Monument, USS Constitution, Faneuil Hall, Old State House.
- **Accessibility:** Faneuil Hall Visitor Center, Bunker Hill Museum, and Charlestown Navy Yard Visitor Center are accessible. Many sites along the Freedom Trail have accessible entrances.
- **Visitor Centers:**
  - Faneuil Hall Visitor Center: Dock Square, Boston, MA. Open daily 10am–5pm.
  - Bunker Hill Museum: 43 Monument Square, Charlestown, MA. Open Wed–Sun, 1pm–5pm.
  - Charlestown Navy Yard Visitor Center: Charlestown Navy Yard, Boston, MA. Open Wed–Sun, 10am–5pm.
- **Contact:** 617-242-5601 | bost_rangers@nps.gov

---
## 5. Cape Cod National Seashore (Cape Cod, MA)
- **Highlights:** Historic lighthouses, cultural landscapes, museum exhibits, accessible beaches and trails.
- **Accessibility:** Province Lands Visitor Center is accessible and open mid-May to mid-October, 9am–5pm. Accessible restrooms and observation decks. Some beaches and trails have beach wheelchairs and accessible paths.
- **Current Alerts:**
  - Cashless payments only at entrance stations starting July 1.
  - Salt Pond Visitor Center phone lines are down; use alternate number for reservations.
- **Visitor Center:** 171 Race Point Road, Provincetown, MA.
- **Contact:** (508) 487-1256 | caco_superintendent@nps.gov

---
## 6. Frederick Law Olmsted National Historic Site (Brookline, MA)
- **Highlights:** Home and office of America’s foremost landscape architect, museum exhibits, gardens.
- **Accessibility:** Contact ahead for accessibility details; grounds are open dawn to dusk.
- **Visitor Center:** 99 Warren Street, Brookline, MA.
- **Contact:** 617-566-1689 | frla_interpretation@nps.gov

---
## 7. John Fitzgerald Kennedy National Historic Site (Brookline, MA)
- **Highlights:** Birthplace and childhood home of JFK, museum exhibits.
- **Accessibility:** Contact ahead for accessibility details. Some tours may be unavailable due to group reservations (July 17, 10am; July 25, 3pm).
- **Visitor Center:** 83 Beals Street, Brookline, MA. Open Thurs–Sun, 10am–5pm

final_response:
Here’s a detailed plan for an accessible wildlife watching and camping weekend in Alaska’s national parks, focusing on accessibility, wildlife opportunities, campground options, alerts, events, and visitor center resources for June 20–22, 2025:

---
## 1. Park Selection & Wildlife Watching

The following Alaska national parks offer wildlife watching opportunities:
- **Alagnak Wild River**
- **Aleutian Islands World War II National Historic Area**
- **Aniakchak National Monument & Preserve**
- **Bering Land Bridge National Preserve**

All these parks are known for their wildlife and natural beauty, but accessibility and facilities vary greatly due to their remote nature.

---
## 2. Campground Options

- None of these parks have developed, reservable campgrounds. Camping is generally backcountry or primitive, and accessibility accommodations are extremely limited. If accessible camping is a priority, consider contacting the King Salmon Visitor Center (for Alagnak and Aniakchak) or the park directly for advice on possible arrangements.

---
## 3. Park Alerts (Closures & Hazards)

**Bering Land Bridge National Preserve:**
- Unsafe Airstrip Conditions at Serpentine Hot Springs—airstrip is wet, rutted, and not recommended for use.
- Visitor Center is closed for renovations, but staff are available by phone/email.
- Outhouse is out of order—visitors must use Leave No Trace methods.
- Phone lines may be intermittent—use email if needed.

No current alerts for the other parks, but always check before traveling due to Alaska’s rapidly changing conditions.

---
## 4. Ranger-Led Wildlife Events (June 20–22, 2025)

- No ranger-led wildlife events are currently scheduled for these dates in these parks. Check with visitor centers closer to your visit for updates, as events may be added.

---
## 5. Visitor Centers (for Accessibility & Information)

- **King Salmon Visitor Center** (serves Alagnak Wild River & Aniakchak NM&P)
  - Location: Next to King Salmon Airport, King Salmon, AK 99613
  - Hours: Daily, 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM (from June 1)
  - Contact: 907-246-4250 | KATM_Visitor_Information@nps.gov
  - Accessibility: Contact for details on accessible facilities and trip planning.

- **Aleutian WWII National Historic Area Visitor Center**
  - Location: 2716 Airport Beach Road, Unalaska, AK 99865
  - Hours: Daily, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM (summer)
  - Contact: (907) 581-9944 | aerology@arctic.net

- **Bering Land Bridge Visitor Center** (Nome, AK)
  - Location: 214 Front Street, Sitnasuak Building, Nome, AK 99762
  - Hours: Wed–Sat, 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM (closed Mon/Sun)
  - Contact: 1-800-471-2352 | bela_interpretation@nps.gov
  - Note: Currently closed for renovations; staff available by phone/email.

---
## 6. Itinerary Suggestions

### Friday, June 20
- Arrive in King Salmon or Nome (depending on park choice).
- Visit the local visitor center for accessibility info, maps, and wildlife updates.
- Set up primitive/backcountry camp (contact visitor center for best accessible options).

### Saturday, June 21
- Wildlife watching (river, tundra, or coastal areas—ask rangers for best accessible spots).
- Explore interpretive trails or self-guided tours if available.
- Check for any pop-up ranger programs at the visitor center.

### Sunday, June 22
- Morning wildlife viewing.
- Pack up camp and return to visitor center for feedback and further exploration.

---
## 7. Accessibility Notes

- Developed accessible facilities are extremely limited in these remote parks.
- Visitor centers are your best resource for up-to-date accessibility information and possible accommodations.
- Contact the centers in advance to discuss your group’s needs.

---
## 8. Recommendations

- For the best combination of accessibility and wildlife, base your trip out of King Salmon (serving Alagnak Wild River and Aniakchak NM&P) and use the King Salmon Visitor Center as your hub.
- Always check for updated alerts and contact visitor centers before your trip.
- Be prepared for primitive camping and bring all necessary supplies.

Here’s a comprehensive plan for your Wisconsin national park family reunion focused on water recreation, including park options, safety alerts, campground details, and event availability for July 18–20, 2025:

—
Best National Parks in Wisconsin for Water Recreation

1. Apostle Islands National Lakeshore (Park Code: apis)
   - Activities: Boating, kayaking, sailing, fishing, swimming, camping, guided tours, and more.
   - Highlights: 21 scenic islands, sea caves, sandy beaches, lighthouses, and Lake Superior shoreline.
   - Website: [Apostle Islands NLS](https://www.nps.gov/apis/index.htm)
   - Safety Alerts:
     - Devil’s Island marina and campsite closed for construction summer 2025.
     - Some area closures (Devils Island dock, West Bay Club, trail on Stockton Island).
     - Bear activity—follow food storage and safety guidelines.
     - Meyers Beach parking is digital payment only.
     - Some private inholdings are closed to the public.
   - Campgrounds: No NPS-managed campgrounds listed in the database, but backcountry and island camping is available (check park website for details).
   - Events: No water-related events listed for your dates.

2. Saint Croix National Scenic Riverway (Park Code: sacn)
   - Activities: Boating, canoeing, kayaking, fishing, tubing, swimming, camping.
   - Highlights: Over 200 miles of clean, scenic river (St. Croix and Namekagon), forested landscapes, wildlife.
   - Website: [St. Croix NSR](https://www.nps.gov/sacn/index.htm)
   - Safety Alerts:
     - Increased bear activity along the Namekagon River—store food properly.
   - Campgrounds:
     - Lower St. Croix District: 19 primitive, first-come, first-served campsites (permit required, no water, not ADA accessible).
     - Middle St. Croix: 57 primitive, free, first-come, first-served campsites.
     - Namekagon District: 67 primitive, free, first-come, first-served campsites.
     - All sites are tent-only, group sites available, no potable water, bring your own toilet supplies.
     - More info: [Camping on the Riverway](https://www.nps.gov/sacn/planyourvisit/camping.htm)
   - Events: No water-related events listed for your dates.

3. Ice Age National Scenic Trail (Park Code: iatr)
   - Activities: Fishing, camping, hiking, wildlife watching.
   - Highlights: 1,200-mile trail across Wisconsin’s glacial landscape.
   - Website: [Ice Age NST](https://www.nps.gov/iatr/index.htm)
   - Safety Alerts:
     - Trail conditions vary—check the Ice Age Trail Alliance website for updates: [Trail Conditions](https://iceagetrail.maps.arcgis.com/apps/opsdashboard/index.html#/5cb8ca63f0e447dea9dc29afb5ed12e6)
   - Campgrounds: No NPS-managed campgrounds listed; some segments allow backcountry camping (check local regulations).
   - Events: No water-related events listed for your dates.

4. North Country National Scenic Trail (Park Code: noco)
   - Activities: Hiking, camping, wildlife watching.
   - Highlights: Crosses northern Wisconsin, connects lakes and streams.
   - Website: [North Country NST](https://www.nps.gov/noco/index.htm)
   - Safety Alerts:
     - Trail closures possible—check [NCTA Trail Alerts](https://northcountrytrail.org/the-trail/trail-alerts/)
   - Campgrounds: No NPS-managed campgrounds listed; some backcountry camping possible.
   - Events: No water-related events listed for your dates.

—
Recommendations for Your Family Reunion

- Top Choice: Saint Croix National Scenic Riverway
  - Best for large groups, easy access to water recreation (boating, fishing, swimming, tubing), and multiple primitive campgrounds.
  - Ample first-come, first-served campsites for tents and groups.
  - Be bear aware—store food properly.
  - No water-related events scheduled, but the river itself offers plenty of recreation.

- Runner-Up: Apostle Islands National Lakeshore
  - Ideal for adventurous families interested in island camping, kayaking, and exploring Lake Superior.

—
Best National Parks in Wisconsin for Water Recreation

1. Apostle Islands National Lakeshore (Park Code: apis)
   - Activities: Boating, kayaking, sailing, fishing, swimming, camping, guided tours, and more.
   - Highlights: 21 scenic islands, sea caves, sandy beaches, lighthouses, and Lake Superior shoreline.
   - Website: [Apostle Islands NLS](https://www.nps.gov/apis/index.htm)
   - Safety Alerts:
     - Devil’s Island marina and campsite closed for construction summer 2025.
     - Some area closures (Devils Island dock, West Bay Club, trail on Stockton Island).
     - Bear activity—follow food storage and safety guidelines.
     - Meyers Beach parking is digital payment only.
     - Some private inholdings are closed to the public.
   - Campgrounds: No NPS-managed campgrounds listed in the database, but backcountry and island camping is available (check park website for details).
   - Events: No water-related events listed for your dates.

2. Saint Croix National Scenic Riverway (Park Code: sacn)
   - Activities: Boating, canoeing, kayaking, fishing, tubing, swimming, camping.
   - Highlights: Over 200 miles of clean, scenic river (St. Croix and Namekagon), forested landscapes, wildlife.
   - Website: [St. Croix NSR](https://www.nps.gov/sacn/index.htm)
   - Safety Alerts:
     - Increased bear activity along the Namekagon River—store food properly.
   - Campgrounds:
     - Lower St. Croix District: 19 primitive, first-come, first-served campsites (permit required, no water, not ADA accessible).
     - Middle St. Croix: 57 primitive, free, first-come, first-served campsites.
     - Namekagon District: 67 primitive, free, first-come, first-served campsites.
     - All sites are tent-only, group sites available, no potable water, bring your own toilet supplies.
     - More info: [Camping on the Riverway](https://www.nps.gov/sacn/planyourvisit/camping.htm)
   - Events: No water-related events listed for your dates.

3. Ice Age National Scenic Trail (Park Code: iatr)
   - Activities: Fishing, camping, hiking, wildlife watching.
   - Highlights: 1,200-mile trail across Wisconsin’s glacial landscape.
