final_response:
Here is a comprehensive plan for a National Park Wellness and Mindfulness Retreat in Vermont, focusing on relaxation, meditation, and nature immersion:

—
PARK SELECTION

1. Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller National Historical Park (MABI)
   - Location: Woodstock, VT
   - Highlights: 20 miles of scenic trails and carriage roads through the Mount Tom Forest, historic gardens, and a focus on conservation and stewardship.
   - Activities: Hiking, nature walks, guided tours, wildlife watching, birdwatching, and cultural programs.
   - Website: https://www.nps.gov/mabi/index.htm

2. Appalachian National Scenic Trail (APPA) – Vermont Section
   - Highlights: The Vermont section of the Appalachian Trail offers wooded paths, mountain views, and opportunities for hiking and nature immersion.
   - Activities: Hiking, backcountry hiking, wildlife watching, birdwatching.
   - Website: https://www.nps.gov/appa/index.htm

3. North Country National Scenic Trail (NOCO) – Vermont Section
   - Highlights: Connects scenic, natural, and historic areas, offering hiking and nature immersion.
   - Activities: Hiking, wildlife watching, birdwatching.
   - Website: https://www.nps.gov/noco/index.htm

—
SAFETY & ALERTS

- Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller NHP: No emergency alerts. Note that the park is cashless; only credit/debit cards are accepted for tours.
- Appalachian Trail: Some trail closures remain post-Hurricane Helene. Check https://appalachiantrail.org/trail-updates/ for up-to-date info. Be aware of black bears in some areas (mainly Virginia).
- North Country Trail: Occasional trail closures; check https://northcountrytrail.org/the-trail/trail-alerts/ for updates.

—
VISITOR CENTERS

Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller NHP:
- Carriage Barn Visitor Center (on-site): Open Thursday–Monday, 10am–5pm (during your retreat dates). Offers orientation, exhibits, bookstore, and program sign-ups.
  - Address: 69 Old River Rd, Woodstock, VT 05091
  - Phone: 802-457-3368 x0
  - Email: mabi_visitorservices@nps.gov

- Billings Farm & Museum Visitor Center (adjacent): Open daily, 10am–5pm.
  - Address: 69 Old River Rd, Woodstock, VT 05091
  - Phone: (802) 457-2355
  - Email: info@billingsfarm.org

Appalachian Trail & North Country Trail:
- No dedicated visitor centers in Vermont, but the Appalachian Trail Conservancy provides resources online and at out-of-state centers.

—
CAMPING & ACCOMMODATION

- There are no developed campgrounds within Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller NHP.
- The Appalachian and North Country Trails offer backcountry camping and shelters along the trail (primitive, hike-in only). For group camping, consider nearby state parks or private campgrounds in the Woodstock area.
- For a more comfortable retreat, local inns, lodges, or group rentals in Woodstock are recommended.

—
EVENTS (July 10–13, 2025)

- No official wellness, meditation, or mindfulness events are currently scheduled in these parks during your retreat dates.
- However, Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller NHP often offers ranger-led walks and nature programs. Check their website or contact the visitor center closer to your dates for updated offerings.

—
RECOMMENDED RETREAT ITINERARY

Day 1: Arrival & Orientation
- Arrive in Woodstock, VT.
- Visit the Carriage Barn Visitor Center for orientation and trail maps.
- Gentle nature walk in the park’s gardens and forest trails.

Day 2: Mindfulness & Nature Immersion

Here is a comprehensive plan for a National Park Wellness and Mindfulness Retreat in Vermont, focusing on relaxation, meditation, and nature immersion:

—
PARK SELECTION

1. Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller National Historical Park (MABI)
   - Location: Woodstock, VT
   - Highlights: 20 miles of scenic trails and carriage roads through the Mount Tom Forest, historic gardens, and a focus on conservation and stewardship.
   - Activities: Hiking, nature walks, guided tours, wildlife watching, birdwatching, and cultural programs.
   - Website: https://www.nps.gov/mabi/index.htm

2. Appalachian National Scenic Trail (APPA) – Vermont Section
   - Highlights: The Vermont section of the Appalachian Trail offers wooded paths, mountain views, and opportunities for hiking and nature immersion.
   - Activities: Hiking, backcountry hiking, wildlife watching, birdwatching.
   - Website: https://www.nps.gov/appa/index.htm

3. North Country National Scenic Trail (NOCO) – Vermont Section
   - Highlights: Connects scenic, natural, and historic areas, offering hiking and nature immersion.
   - Activities: Hiking, wildlife watching, birdwatching.
   - Website: https://www.nps.gov/noco/index.htm

—
SAFETY & ALERTS

- Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller NHP: No emergency alerts. Note that the park is cashless; only credit/debit cards are accepted for tours.
- Appalachian Trail: Some trail closures remain post-Hurricane Helene. Check https://appalachiantrail.org/trail-updates/ for up-to-date info. Be aware of black bears in some areas (mainly Virginia).
- North Country Trail: Occasional trail closures; check https://northcountrytrail.org/the-trail/trail-alerts/ for updates.

—
VISITOR CENTERS

Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller NHP:
- Carriage Barn Visitor Center (on-site): Open Thursday–Monday, 10am–5pm (during your retreat dates). Offers orientation, exhibits, bookstore, and program sign-ups.
  - Address: 69 Old River Rd, Woodstock, VT 05091
  - Phone: 802-457-3368 x0
  - Email: mabi_visitorservices@nps.gov

- Billings Farm & Museum Visitor Center (adjacent): Open daily, 10am–5pm.
  - Address: 69 Old River Rd, Woodstock, VT 05091
  - Phone: (802) 457-2355
  - Email: info@billingsfarm.org

Appalachian Trail & North Country Trail:
- No dedicated visitor centers in Vermont, but the Appalachian Trail Conservancy provides resources online and at out-of-state centers.

—
CAMPING & ACCOMMODATION

- There are no developed campgrounds within Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller NHP.
- The Appalachian and North Country Trails offer backcountry camping and shelters along the trail (primitive, hike-in only). For group camping, consider nearby state parks or private campgrounds in the Woodstock area.
- For a more comfortable retreat, local inns, lodges, or group rentals in Woodstock are recommended.

—
EVENTS (July 10–13, 2025)

- No official wellness, meditation, or mindfulness events are currently scheduled in these parks during your retreat dates.

- Morning guided hike on Mount Tom trails.
- Group meditation session in a scenic forest clearing.

Day 4: Closing & Departure
- Sunrise walk or yoga in the park.
- Closing circle and departure.

final_response:
Here is a comprehensive itinerary for a fossil and paleontology exploration trip to Badlands National Park, South Dakota, from July 15–20, 2025:

—
**1. Park Overview: Badlands National Park**
- Website: [Badlands National Park](https://www.nps.gov/badl/index.htm)
- Description: Renowned for one of the world’s richest fossil beds, Badlands preserves ancient mammal fossils (horses, rhinos, etc.) and dramatic geologic formations. The park covers 244,000 acres of mixed-grass prairie and rugged badlands.
- Location: 25216 Ben Reifel Road, Interior, SD 57750 (75 miles east of Rapid City)
- Weather: Hot, dry summers with possible violent thunderstorms; be prepared for variable conditions.
- Entrance Fees: $30/vehicle (7 days), $15/person (hiking/biking), $55 annual pass.

—
**2. Current Alerts**
- Conata Picnic Ground is temporarily closed due to construction.
- Do not rely on GPS navigation; use the official address for the Ben Reifel Visitor Center.

—
**3. Visitor Centers with Educational Exhibits**
- **Ben Reifel Visitor Center**
  - Address: 25216 Ben Reifel Road, Interior, SD 57750
  - Hours: 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM daily
  - Features: Fossil exhibits, air-conditioned theater, restrooms, educational programs.
  - Contact: 605-433-5361 | badlands_info@nps.gov
  - Details: [Visit Ben Reifel Visitor Center](https://www.nps.gov/thingstodo/visit-ben-reifel.htm)

- **White River Visitor Center**
  - Address: 2734 BIA 2, Porcupine, SD 57772 (Pine Ridge Reservation)
  - Hours: 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM daily (summer only)
  - Features: Exhibits, info desk, restrooms, picnic tables, impromptu talks.
  - Contact: 605-455-2878

—
**4. Campgrounds**
- **Cedar Pass Campground**
  - Near Ben Reifel Visitor Center; 96 sites (tent/RV/group)
  - Amenities: Flush toilets, coin showers (summer), potable water, amphitheater, accessible sites.
  - Fees: $37/night (tent/RV), $47/night (RV electric), $40/group
  - Reservations: [Reserve at Recreation.gov](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/10288228?tab=campsites)
  - Contact: 605-433-5460

- **Sage Creek Campground**
  - Primitive, free, first-come, first-served (22 sites)
  - No water; pit toilets, picnic tables, horse area
  - RVs/trailers limited to 18 ft; road may be impassable after rain
  - Details: [Sage Creek Campground Info](https://www.nps.gov/thingstodo/backcountry-camping-badl.htm)

—
**5. Paleontology-Related Events (July 15–20, 2025)**
- No specific paleontology or fossil events are currently scheduled for these dates.
- However, the Ben Reifel Visitor Center offers fossil exhibits and may have ranger-led talks or programs—check closer to your visit or inquire at the visitor center.

—
**6. Additional Tips**
- The park is open year-round, but always check for weather-related closures.
- For fossil enthusiasts, the Fossil Exhibit Trail is a must-see, featuring fossil replicas and interpretive signs.
- Contact the park or visitor center ahead of your trip for updates on ranger programs or special paleontology activities.

—
**Sample Itinerary Outline**
- Day 1: Arrive, set up camp at Cedar Pass or Sage Creek, orientation at Ben Reifel Visitor Center.
- Day 2: Explore Fossil Exhibit Trail, attend any available ranger talks, visit exhibits.
- Day 3: Hike additional trails, wildlife viewing, photography.
- Day 4: Visit White River Visitor Center, explore southern park areas.
- Day 5: Free exploration, revisit favorite sites, pack up.

Would you like a printable itinerary or more details about specific trails, fossil sites, or educational programs?

Here is a comprehensive itinerary for a fossil and paleontology exploration trip to Badlands National Park, South Dakota, from July 15–20, 2025:

—
**1. Park Overview: Badlands National Park**
- Website: [Badlands National Park](https://www.nps.gov/badl/index.htm)
- Description: Renowned for one of the world’s richest fossil beds, Badlands preserves ancient mammal fossils (horses, rhinos, etc.) and dramatic geologic formations. The park covers 244,000 acres of mixed-grass prairie and rugged badlands.
- Location: 25216 Ben Reifel Road, Interior, SD 57750 (75 miles east of Rapid City)
- Weather: Hot, dry summers with possible violent thunderstorms; be prepared for variable conditions.
- Entrance Fees: $30/vehicle (7 days), $15/person (hiking/biking), $55 annual pass.

—
**2. Current Alerts**
- Conata Picnic Ground is temporarily closed due to construction.
- Do not rely on GPS navigation; use the official address for the Ben Reifel Visitor Center.

—
**3. Visitor Centers with Educational Exhibits**
- **Ben Reifel Visitor Center**
  - Address: 25216 Ben Reifel Road, Interior, SD 57750
  - Hours: 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM daily
  - Features: Fossil exhibits, air-conditioned theater, restrooms, educational programs.
  - Contact: 605-433-5361 | badlands_info@nps.gov
  - Details: [Visit Ben Reifel Visitor Center](https://www.nps.gov/thingstodo/visit-ben-reifel.htm)

- **White River Visitor Center**
  - Address: 2734 BIA 2, Porcupine, SD 57772 (Pine Ridge Reservation)
  - Hours: 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM daily (summer only)
  - Features: Exhibits, info desk, restrooms, picnic tables, impromptu talks.
  - Contact: 605-455-2878

—
**4. Campgrounds**
- **Cedar Pass Campground**
  - Near Ben Reifel Visitor Center; 96 sites (tent/RV/group)
  - Amenities: Flush toilets, coin showers (summer), potable water, amphitheater, accessible sites.
  - Fees: $37/night (tent/RV), $47/night (RV electric), $40/group
  - Reservations: [Reserve at Recreation.gov](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/10288228?tab=campsites)
  - Contact: 605-433-5460

- **Sage Creek Campground**
  - Primitive, free, first-come, first-served (22 sites)
  - No water; pit toilets, picnic tables, horse area
  - RVs/trailers limited to 18 ft; road may be impassable after rain
  - Details: [Sage Creek Campground Info](https://www.nps.gov/thingstodo/backcountry-camping-badl.htm)

—
**5. Paleontology-Related Events (July 15–20, 2025)**
- No specific paleontology or fossil events are currently scheduled for these dates.
- However, the Ben Reifel Visitor Center offers fossil exhibits and may have ranger-led talks or programs—check closer to your visit or inquire at the visitor center.

—
**6. Additional Tips**
- The park is open year-round, but always check for weather-related closures.
- For fossil enthusiasts, the Fossil Exhibit Trail is a must-see, featuring fossil replicas and interpretive signs.
- Contact the park or visitor center ahead of your trip for updates on ranger programs or special paleontology activities.

—
**Sample Itinerary Outline**
- Day 1: Arrive, set up camp at Cedar Pass or Sage Creek, orientation at Ben Reifel Visitor Center.
- Day 2: Explore Fossil Exhibit Trail, attend any available ranger talks, visit exhibits.
- Day 3: Hike additional trails, wildlife viewing, photography.
- Day 4: Visit White River Visitor Center, explore southern park areas.
- Day 5: Free exploration, revisit favorite sites, pack up.

final_response:
Here is a comprehensive plan for your National Park Wellness and Forest Bathing Retreat in Shenandoah National Park for June 2025:

1. Park Suitability for Wellness & Forest Bathing
- Shenandoah National Park is an ideal location for a wellness and forest bathing retreat. It features lush forests, abundant hiking trails, and a tranquil natural environment perfect for mindfulness, nature immersion, and wellness activities.
- The park is renowned for its scenic beauty, biodiversity, and opportunities for solitude and reflection, making it highly suitable for forest bathing and mindfulness retreats.

2. Campground Availability for Overnight Stays
All major campgrounds in Shenandoah will be open in June 2025:
- Big Meadows Campground (mile 51.2): Centrally located, 221 sites (220 reservable), group sites available. Reservations are required and can be made via Recreation.gov. Amenities include flush toilets, showers, laundry, camp store, and ADA-accessible sites. More info & reservations: Big Meadows Campground
- Lewis Mountain Campground (mile 57.5): Small, quiet, 30 first-come, first-served sites. No reservations. Amenities include flush toilets, showers, laundry, and ADA-accessible sites. More info: Lewis Mountain Campground
- Loft Mountain Campground (mile 79.5): Large, scenic, 207 sites (141 reservable, 50 first-come, first-served). Amenities include flush toilets, showers, laundry, camp store, and ADA-accessible sites. Reservations: Loft Mountain Campground
- Mathews Arm Campground (mile 22.1): Northernmost, 165 sites (112 reservable, 47 first-come, first-served), group sites available. Amenities include flush toilets, laundry, and ADA-accessible sites. Reservations: Mathews Arm Campground

3. Park Alerts Affecting Access or Activities (as of June 2025)
- The park is fully cashless at entrance stations as of July 1, 2025—only cards or mobile payments accepted.
- Charging stations at Skyland are out of service.
- Parking at boundary access areas is strictly enforced; park only in designated areas to avoid towing.
- There may be delays on Skyline Drive between miles 72.8 and 75.7 due to stone wall rehabilitation (single lane closure).
- A day-use ticket is required to hike Old Rag (March 1–Nov 30). Details: Old Rag Ticket Info
- For real-time Skyline Drive status and closures, check: Skyline Drive Status

4. Visitor Centers for Orientation & Indoor Sessions
- Dickey Ridge Visitor Center (mile 4.6): Near Front Royal, ideal for northern park orientation. Facilities: restrooms, bookstore, maps, and information. Open daily, 9am–5pm (Fri/Sat until 6pm).
  Address: 17065 Skyline Drive, Front Royal, VA 22630
- Harry F. Byrd Sr. Visitor Center (mile 51): Central location across from Big Meadows. Facilities: restrooms, ranger programs, bookstore, first aid. Open daily, 9am–5pm (Fri/Sat until 6pm).
  Address: 259 Big Meadows Visitor Road, Stanley, VA 22851

5. Upcoming Wellness or Mindfulness Events (June 10–20, 2025)
- No official wellness, mindfulness, or forest bathing events are currently scheduled in Shenandoah National Park for June 10–20, 2025. You may wish to coordinate directly with park staff to propose or list your retreat as an official event.

Summary for Promotion & Planning
- Shenandoah National Park is highly suitable for a wellness and forest bathing retreat, with ample natural beauty, trails, and tranquil spaces.
- Multiple campgrounds are available for group and individual overnight stays, with both reservable and first-come, first-served options.
- No major closures or hazards are expected in June 2025, but be aware of cashless entry, parking rules, and possible minor delays on Skyline Drive.
- Two main visitor centers offer excellent facilities for orientation, indoor sessions, and group gatherings.
- No conflicting events are scheduled during your planned retreat dates.

For further coordination, contact the park at shen_info@nps.gov or (540) 999-3500.

Would you like a sample retreat itinerary or additional recommendations for forest bathing locations and activities within the park?

Here is a comprehensive plan for your National Park Wellness and Forest Bathing Retreat in Shenandoah National Park for June 2025:

1. Park Suitability for Wellness & Forest Bathing
- Shenandoah National Park is an ideal location for a wellness and forest bathing retreat. It features lush forests, abundant hiking trails, and a tranquil natural environment perfect for mindfulness, nature immersion, and wellness activities.
- The park is renowned for its scenic beauty, biodiversity, and opportunities for solitude and reflection, making it highly suitable for forest bathing and mindfulness retreats.

2. Campground Availability for Overnight Stays
All major campgrounds in Shenandoah will be open in June 2025:
- Big Meadows Campground (mile 51.2): Centrally located, 221 sites (220 reservable), group sites available. Reservations are required and can be made via Recreation.gov. Amenities include flush toilets, showers, laundry, camp store, and ADA-accessible sites. More info & reservations: Big Meadows Campground
- Lewis Mountain Campground (mile 57.5): Small, quiet, 30 first-come, first-served sites. No reservations. Amenities include flush toilets, showers, laundry, and ADA-accessible sites. More info: Lewis Mountain Campground
- Loft Mountain Campground (mile 79.5): Large, scenic, 207 sites (141 reservable, 50 first-come, first-served). Amenities include flush toilets, showers, laundry, camp store, and ADA-accessible sites. Reservations: Loft Mountain Campground
- Mathews Arm Campground (mile 22.1): Northernmost, 165 sites (112 reservable, 47 first-come, first-served), group sites available. Amenities include flush toilets, laundry, and ADA-accessible sites. Reservations: Mathews Arm Campground

3. Park Alerts Affecting Access or Activities (as of June 2025)
- The park is fully cashless at entrance stations as of July 1, 2025—only cards or mobile payments accepted.
- Charging stations at Skyland are out of service.
- Parking at boundary access areas is strictly enforced; park only in designated areas to avoid towing.
- There may be delays on Skyline Drive between miles 72.8 and 75.7 due to stone wall rehabilitation (single lane closure).
- A day-use ticket is required to hike Old Rag (March 1–Nov 30). Details: Old Rag Ticket Info
- For real-time Skyline Drive status and closures, check: Skyline Drive Status

4. Visitor Centers for Orientation & Indoor Sessions
- Dickey Ridge Visitor Center (mile 4.6): Near Front Royal, ideal for northern park orientation. Facilities: restrooms, bookstore, maps, and information. Open daily, 9am–5pm (Fri/Sat until 6pm).
  Address: 17065 Skyline Drive, Front Royal, VA 22630
- Harry F. Byrd Sr. Visitor Center (mile 51): Central location across from Big Meadows. Facilities: restrooms, ranger programs, bookstore, first aid. Open daily, 9am–5pm (Fri/Sat until 6pm).
  Address: 259 Big Meadows Visitor Road, Stanley, VA 22851

5. Upcoming Wellness or Mindfulness Events (June 10–20, 2025)
- No official wellness, mindfulness, or forest bathing events are currently scheduled in Shenandoah National Park for June 10–20, 2025. You may wish to coordinate directly with park staff to propose or list your retreat as an official event.

Summary for Promotion & Planning
- Shenandoah National Park is highly suitable for a wellness and forest bathing retreat, with ample natural beauty, trails, and tranquil spaces.
- Multiple campgrounds are available for group and individual overnight stays, with both reservable and first-come, first-served options.
- No major closures or hazards are expected in June 2025, but be aware of cashless entry, parking rules, and possible minor delays on Skyline Drive.
- Two main visitor centers offer excellent facilities for orientation, indoor sessions, and group gatherings.
- No conflicting events are scheduled during your planned retreat dates.

For further coordination, contact the park at shen_info@nps.gov or (540) 999-3500.

final_response:
Here’s a comprehensive plan for a National Park Wildlife Rehabilitation Volunteer Experience in California, focusing on parks with wildlife viewing and conservation activities, and including essential logistics for your July 2025 trip:

---

## 1. Top California National Parks for Wildlife & Conservation

The following parks offer wildlife viewing, conservation, and related activities:

- **Channel Islands National Park (CHIS)**
- **Golden Gate National Recreation Area (GOGA)**
- **Lassen Volcanic National Park (LAVO)**
- **Mojave National Preserve (MOJA)**
- **Joshua Tree National Park (JOTR)**
- **Death Valley National Park (DEVA)**
- **Muir Woods National Monument (MUWO)**
- **Lava Beds National Monument (LABE)**

---

## 2. Volunteer, Wildlife, and Conservation Events (July 1–15, 2025)

- **No official volunteer or wildlife rehabilitation events are currently scheduled in these parks for July 1–15, 2025.**
  - For hands-on wildlife rehabilitation, consider contacting park staff directly or local conservation organizations for special opportunities.

---

## 3. Important Alerts & Conditions

- **Lassen Volcanic (LAVO):**
  - Bumpass Hell Trail closed due to snow (likely until mid-July).
  - Juniper Lake Road closed due to fire damage.
- **Death Valley (DEVA):**
  - Event: Runners on CA Hwy 190 (July 7–9) – drive carefully.
  - Fire restrictions: No open flame fires at certain campgrounds.
- **Mojave (MOJA):**
  - Fire restrictions: No wood/charcoal fires; camp stoves allowed.
  - Some roads are rough/damaged; 4WD recommended in places.
- **Golden Gate (GOGA):**
  - Marin Headlands Chapel area closed (June–Sept 2025).
  - China Beach construction (starting July 2025).
- **Joshua Tree (JOTR):**
  - Some campgrounds and 49 Palms Trail closed for summer.
  - Parkwide fire restrictions (no open fires).
- **Channel Islands (CHIS):**
  - Western gulls nesting on Anacapa Island (April–mid-August): expect noise, odor, and aggressive birds.

---

## 4. Campgrounds (Sample Options)

- **Channel Islands (CHIS):** Anacapa Island Campground – primitive, $15/night, reservations required, no water.
- **Lassen Volcanic (LAVO):** Backcountry camping with permit, Butte Lake Campground (reservations required).
- **Joshua Tree (JOTR):** Belle Campground (first-come, first-served), Black Rock and Cottonwood Campgrounds (reservations required).
- **Golden Gate (GOGA):** Bicentennial Campground (near San Francisco, reservations required).
- **Mojave (MOJA):** Black Canyon Group and Equestrian Campground (reservations required).
- **Death Valley (DEVA):** Emigrant Campground (free, first-come, first-served), Eureka Dunes Campground (primitive, 4WD access).

---

## 5. Visitor Centers

- **Channel Islands:** Robert J. Lagomarsino Visitor Center, Ventura (8:30am–5pm).
- **Lassen Volcanic:** Loomis Museum & Kohm Yah-mah-nee Visitor Center.
- **Joshua Tree:** Black Rock Nature Center, Cottonwood Visitor Center, Joshua Tree Visitor Center (varied hours).
- **Golden Gate:** Golden Gate Bridge Welcome Center (9am–6pm).
- **Mojave:** Hole-in-the-Wall Information Center (Fri–Mon, 10am–4pm), Barstow Headquarters.
- **Death Valley:** Furnace Creek Visitor Center (8am–5pm).

---

## 6. Recommendations for Your Trip

- **Contact park staff** for potential volunteer or citizen science opportunities not listed in the public events calendar.
- **Prepare for fire restrictions** and possible closures—especially in summer.
- **Reserve campgrounds early** where required, and bring all necessary supplies (especially water for Channel Islands and desert parks).
- **Check each park’s website** for updated alerts and possible pop-up volunteer events as your trip approaches.

---

### Useful Links

- [Channel Islands National Park](https://www.nps.gov/chis/index.htm)
- [Joshua Tree National Park](https://www.nps.gov/jotr/index.htm)
- [Lassen Volcanic National Park](https://www.nps.gov/lavo/index.htm)
- [Mojave National Preserve](https://www.nps.gov/moja/index.htm)
- [Golden Gate National Recreation Area](https://www.nps.gov/g

Here’s a comprehensive plan for a National Park Wildlife Rehabilitation Volunteer Experience in California, focusing on parks with wildlife viewing and conservation activities, and including essential logistics for your July 2025 trip:

---

## 1. Top California National Parks for Wildlife & Conservation

The following parks offer wildlife viewing, conservation, and related activities:

- **Channel Islands National Park (CHIS)**
- **Golden Gate National Recreation Area (GOGA)**
- **Lassen Volcanic National Park (LAVO)**
- **Mojave National Preserve (MOJA)**
- **Joshua Tree National Park (JOTR)**
- **Death Valley National Park (DEVA)**
- **Muir Woods National Monument (MUWO)**
- **Lava Beds National Monument (LABE)**

---

## 2. Volunteer, Wildlife, and Conservation Events (July 1–15, 2025)

- **No official volunteer or wildlife rehabilitation events are currently scheduled in these parks for July 1–15, 2025.**
  - For hands-on wildlife rehabilitation, consider contacting park staff directly or local conservation organizations for special opportunities.

---

## 3. Important Alerts & Conditions

- **Lassen Volcanic (LAVO):**
  - Bumpass Hell Trail closed due to snow (likely until mid-July).
  - Juniper Lake Road closed due to fire damage.
- **Death Valley (DEVA):**
  - Event: Runners on CA Hwy 190 (July 7–9) – drive carefully.
  - Fire restrictions: No open flame fires at certain campgrounds.
- **Mojave (MOJA):**
  - Fire restrictions: No wood/charcoal fires; camp stoves allowed.
  - Some roads are rough/damaged; 4WD recommended in places.
- **Golden Gate (GOGA):**
  - Marin Headlands Chapel area closed (June–Sept 2025).
  - China Beach construction (starting July 2025).
- **Joshua Tree (JOTR):**
  - Some campgrounds and 49 Palms Trail closed for summer.
  - Parkwide fire restrictions (no open fires).
- **Channel Islands (CHIS):**
  - Western gulls nesting on Anacapa Island (April–mid-August): expect noise, odor, and aggressive birds.

---

## 4. Campgrounds (Sample Options)

- **Channel Islands (CHIS):** Anacapa Island Campground – primitive, $15/night, reservations required, no water.
- **Lassen Volcanic (LAVO):** Backcountry camping with permit, Butte Lake Campground (reservations required).
- **Joshua Tree (JOTR):** Belle Campground (first-come, first-served), Black Rock and Cottonwood Campgrounds (reservations required).
- **Golden Gate (GOGA):** Bicentennial Campground (near San Francisco, reservations required).
- **Mojave (MOJA):** Black Canyon Group and Equestrian Campground (reservations required).
- **Death Valley (DEVA):** Emigrant Campground (free, first-come, first-served), Eureka Dunes Campground (primitive, 4WD access).

---

## 5. Visitor Centers

- **Channel Islands:** Robert J. Lagomarsino Visitor Center, Ventura (8:30am–5pm).
- **Lassen Volcanic:** Loomis Museum & Kohm Yah-mah-nee Visitor Center.
- **Joshua Tree:** Black Rock Nature Center, Cottonwood Visitor Center, Joshua Tree Visitor Center (varied hours).
- **Golden Gate:** Golden Gate Bridge Welcome Center (9am–6pm).
- **Mojave:** Hole-in-the-Wall Information Center (Fri–Mon, 10am–4pm), Barstow Headquarters.
- **Death Valley:** Furnace Creek Visitor Center (8am–5pm).

---

## 6. Recommendations for Your Trip

- **Contact park staff** for potential volunteer or citizen science opportunities not listed in the public events calendar.
- **Prepare for fire restrictions** and possible closures—especially in summer.
- **Reserve campgrounds early** where required, and bring all necessary supplies (especially water for Channel Islands and desert parks).
- **Check each park’s website** for updated alerts and possible pop-up volunteer events as your trip approaches.

final_response:
Here is a detailed plan for your photography expedition to iconic national parks in Arizona and Utah, focusing on sunrise and sunset landscapes. This summary includes scenic highlights, current alerts, visitor centers, campgrounds, and photography-related events for Bryce Canyon, Capitol Reef, Glen Canyon, and Grand Canyon National Parks.

---

## 1. Bryce Canyon National Park (UT)
- **Scenic Highlights:** Hoodoos, Bryce Amphitheater, Inspiration Point, Sunrise & Sunset Points, Queen’s Garden Trail.
- **Current Alerts:**
  - Park is open, all trails and campgrounds accessible.
  - Some smoky conditions possible—check air quality updates.
  - Fire restrictions in place: https://www.nps.gov/brca/learn/news/interagency-news-release-5-29-2025.htm
- **Visitor Center:** Open daily 8am–8pm in summer. Located on Highway 63, Bryce, UT. Info: 435-834-5322.
- **Campgrounds:** 
  - North and Sunset Campgrounds (details: https://www.nps.gov/brca/planyourvisit/campgrounds.htm).
- **Photography Event:** 
  - Full Moon Hike (typically at sunset, ranger-led, reservations required): https://www.nps.gov/brca/planyourvisit/fullmoonhikes.htm

---

## 2. Capitol Reef National Park (UT)
- **Scenic Highlights:** Waterpocket Fold, Fruita Historic District, Hickman Bridge, Strike Valley, Cathedral Valley.
- **Current Alerts:**
  - Visitor Center closed July 15 (planned outage, staff available outside).
  - Scenic Drive closed beyond Fruita Campground into late July (no access for vehicles, bikes, or pedestrians): https://www.nps.gov/care/planyourvisit/scenic-drive-rehabilitation-project.htm
  - Some canyons closed through 8/31/2025: https://www.nps.gov/care/planyourvisit/canyoneering.htm
- **Visitor Center:** Open daily 8am–4:30pm, 52 West Headquarters Dr, Torrey, UT. Info: 435-425-3791.
- **Campgrounds:** 
  - Fruita Campground (year-round, reservations recommended): https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/272245
  - Backcountry camping with permit (free, available at visitor center).

---

## 3. Glen Canyon National Recreation Area (AZ/UT)
- **Scenic Highlights:** Lake Powell, Horseshoe Bend, Lees Ferry, slot canyons, Rainbow Bridge.
- **Current Alerts:**
  - Harmful algal blooms in Antelope Canyon/Lake Powell—avoid unnecessary water exposure: https://www.nps.gov/glca/learn/news/20250702.htm
  - Stage 1 fire restrictions: https://www.blm.gov/announcement/southwest-utah-northern-arizona-interagency-fire-restrictions
- **Visitor Centers:** 
  - Carl Hayden Visitor Center (Page, AZ, 9am–5pm).
  - Escalante Interagency Visitor Center (Escalante, UT, Tue–Sat 9am–4pm).
  - Bullfrog Visitor Center (seasonal).
- **Campgrounds:** 
  - Antelope Point RV Park (Page, AZ, reservations: https://antelopepointlakepowell.com/explore-lake-powell/rv-park/)
  - Beehives Campground (Page, AZ, first-come, $14/night)
  - Bullfrog RV & Campground (Lake Powell, UT, reservations: https://www.lakepowell.com/rv-camping/bullfrog-rv-campground/)
  - Primitive camping options available.
- **Note:** Summer temperatures can be extreme; plan accordingly.

---

## 4. Grand Canyon National Park (AZ)
- **Scenic Highlights:** South Rim (Mather Point, Yavapai Point, Desert View), North Rim (Cape Royal, Bright Angel Point), Colorado River vistas.
- **Current Alerts:**
  - North Rim: Stage 3 water restrictions due to pump issues—check for updates: https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/north-rim.htm
  - Some trail closures and extreme heat warnings—check daily updates: https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/key-messages.htm
- **Visitor Centers:** 
  - South Rim: Grand Canyon Visitor Center (8am–4pm).
  - North Rim: Visitor Center/Park Store (9am–5pm, seasonal).
- **Campgrounds:** 
  - Desert View Campground (East Entrance, reservations required, $30/night): https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/258825
- **Photography Event:** No specific events during your dates

Here is a detailed plan for your photography expedition to iconic national parks in Arizona and Utah, focusing on sunrise and sunset landscapes. This summary includes scenic highlights, current alerts, visitor centers, campgrounds, and photography-related events for Bryce Canyon, Capitol Reef, Glen Canyon, and Grand Canyon National Parks.

---

## 1. Bryce Canyon National Park (UT)
- **Scenic Highlights:** Hoodoos, Bryce Amphitheater, Inspiration Point, Sunrise & Sunset Points, Queen’s Garden Trail.
- **Current Alerts:**
  - Park is open, all trails and campgrounds accessible.
  - Some smoky conditions possible—check air quality updates.
  - Fire restrictions in place: https://www.nps.gov/brca/learn/news/interagency-news-release-5-29-2025.htm
- **Visitor Center:** Open daily 8am–8pm in summer. Located on Highway 63, Bryce, UT. Info: 435-834-5322.
- **Campgrounds:** 
  - North and Sunset Campgrounds (details: https://www.nps.gov/brca/planyourvisit/campgrounds.htm).
- **Photography Event:** 
  - Full Moon Hike (typically at sunset, ranger-led, reservations required): https://www.nps.gov/brca/planyourvisit/fullmoonhikes.htm

---

## 2. Capitol Reef National Park (UT)
- **Scenic Highlights:** Waterpocket Fold, Fruita Historic District, Hickman Bridge, Strike Valley, Cathedral Valley.
- **Current Alerts:**
  - Visitor Center closed July 15 (planned outage, staff available outside).
  - Scenic Drive closed beyond Fruita Campground into late July (no access for vehicles, bikes, or pedestrians): https://www.nps.gov/care/planyourvisit/scenic-drive-rehabilitation-project.htm
  - Some canyons closed through 8/31/2025: https://www.nps.gov/care/planyourvisit/canyoneering.htm
- **Visitor Center:** Open daily 8am–4:30pm, 52 West Headquarters Dr, Torrey, UT. Info: 435-425-3791.
- **Campgrounds:** 
  - Fruita Campground (year-round, reservations recommended): https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/272245
  - Backcountry camping with permit (free, available at visitor center).

---

## 3. Glen Canyon National Recreation Area (AZ/UT)
- **Scenic Highlights:** Lake Powell, Horseshoe Bend, Lees Ferry, slot canyons, Rainbow Bridge.
- **Current Alerts:**
  - Harmful algal blooms in Antelope Canyon/Lake Powell—avoid unnecessary water exposure: https://www.nps.gov/glca/learn/news/20250702.htm
  - Stage 1 fire restrictions: https://www.blm.gov/announcement/southwest-utah-northern-arizona-interagency-fire-restrictions
- **Visitor Centers:** 
  - Carl Hayden Visitor Center (Page, AZ, 9am–5pm).
  - Escalante Interagency Visitor Center (Escalante, UT, Tue–Sat 9am–4pm).
  - Bullfrog Visitor Center (seasonal).
- **Campgrounds:** 
  - Antelope Point RV Park (Page, AZ, reservations: https://antelopepointlakepowell.com/explore-lake-powell/rv-park/)
  - Beehives Campground (Page, AZ, first-come, $14/night)
  - Bullfrog RV & Campground (Lake Powell, UT, reservations: https://www.lakepowell.com/rv-camping/bullfrog-rv-campground/)
  - Primitive camping options available.
- **Note:** Summer temperatures can be extreme; plan accordingly.

---

## 4. Grand Canyon National Park (AZ)
- **Scenic Highlights:** South Rim (Mather Point, Yavapai Point, Desert View), North Rim (Cape Royal, Bright Angel Point), Colorado River vistas.
- **Current Alerts:**
  - North Rim: Stage 3 water restrictions due to pump issues—check for updates: https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/north-rim.htm
  - Some trail closures and extreme heat warnings—check daily updates: https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/key-messages.htm
- **Visitor Centers:** 
  - South Rim: Grand Canyon Visitor Center (8am–4pm).
  - North Rim: Visitor Center/Park Store (9am–5pm, seasonal).
- **Campgrounds:** 
  - Desert View Campground (East Entrance, reservations required, $30/night): https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/258825
- **Photography Event:** No specific events during your dates

final_response:
Here is a detailed and accessible educational hiking and camping itinerary for a student group in Washington national parks for July 3–7, 2025, focusing on Mount Rainier National Park and Ebey’s Landing National Historical Reserve. Both offer accessible hiking and camping options, educational opportunities, and beautiful natural settings.

---

## 1. Mount Rainier National Park

**Overview:**  
Mount Rainier is an iconic, glaciated volcano with subalpine meadows, ancient forests, and abundant wildlife. It offers accessible trails, educational ranger programs, and group-friendly campgrounds.

### Accessibility Highlights
- Cougar Rock Campground: 4 wheelchair-accessible sites, accessible restrooms, paved roads, and accessible amphitheater.
- White River Campground: Accessible restrooms in Loop C, paved roads, and hard-packed dirt campsites.
- Paradise Area: Henry M. Jackson Visitor Center is accessible, with accessible restrooms and exhibits.
- Many paved or hard-packed trails near Paradise and Longmire are suitable for wheelchairs and mobility devices.

### Campgrounds
- **Cougar Rock Campground** (Recommended for groups)
  - 179 sites, 133 reservable, 5 group sites (tent only), 4 accessible sites.
  - Amenities: flush toilets, potable water, amphitheater, food storage, camp store.
  - Reservations: [Recreation.gov - Cougar Rock](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232466)
  - Fee: $20/night (group sites $60/night)
- **White River Campground**
  - 88 sites, all first-come, first-served, accessible restrooms.
  - Fee: $20/night

### Visitor Centers
- **Henry M. Jackson Memorial Visitor Center (Paradise)**
  - Open daily, 10:00 AM–4:30 PM. Accessible exhibits, restrooms, food, and gift shop.
- **Longmire Museum**
  - Open daily, 9:00 AM–4:30 PM. Accessible, with exhibits and ranger assistance.
- **Sunrise Visitor Center**
  - Open daily in summer, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM. Accessible exhibits and restrooms.

### Educational & Ranger-Led Events (July 3–7, 2025)
- **Paradise Plaza Ranger Program:** Daily, outside the Jackson Visitor Center. Stories, activities, and discussions about the park’s natural and cultural history.
- **Evening Program at Cougar Rock Campground Amphitheater:** July 12 (closest to your dates), ranger-led discussions on Mount Rainier’s human and natural history.
- **Evening Program at Paradise Inn Lobby:** July 11, ranger-led discussions.

### Current Alerts (2025)
- Ohanapecosh Campground and Visitor Center CLOSED for construction.
- Fire ban in effect: No campfires or charcoal grills.
- SR165 Carbon River/Fairfax Bridge closed: No access to Carbon River or Mowich Lake.
- Expect travel delays due to road work and long lines at entrances on weekends.
- Timed entry reservation required for Sunrise Corridor starting July 11 (not needed for your dates).

### Sample Itinerary (July 3–7)
- **Day 1:** Arrive at Cougar Rock Campground, set up camp, orientation, and accessible nature walk.
- **Day 2:** Visit Paradise area, accessible trails (e.g., Nisqually Vista Trail), attend Paradise Plaza Ranger Program.
- **Day 3:** Educational hike near Longmire, visit Longmire Museum, group picnic.
- **Day 4:** Explore accessible trails, attend evening ranger program at Cougar Rock Amphitheater.
- **Day 5:** Pack up, optional short hike or visitor center stop before departure.

---

## 2. Ebey’s Landing National Historical Reserve

**Overview:**  
Located on Whidbey Island, Ebey’s Landing preserves historic farmland, prairies, and coastal bluffs. It offers accessible hiking, group camping, and rich cultural history.

### Accessibility Highlights
- Bluff Trail: Hard-packed dirt, gentle grades, and spectacular views—suitable for many mobility devices.
- Jacob & Sarah Ebey House: Open Thurs–Sun, 10 AM–4 PM in summer.
- Visitor services and accessible restrooms available at state park facilities.

### Campgrounds
- **Fort Casey State Park** and **Fort Ebey State Park** (operated by Washington State Parks)
  - Both offer group and accessible campsites.
  - Reservations: [Washington State Parks Reservations](http://www.parks.wa.gov/)
  - Accessible restrooms and some accessible sites available.

### Visitor Centers
- No dedicated NPS visitor center, but interpretive signs and rangers are present at key sites.
- Administrative office open Mon–Fri, 9 AM–5

Here is a detailed and accessible educational hiking and camping itinerary for a student group in Washington national parks for July 3–7, 2025, focusing on Mount Rainier National Park and Ebey’s Landing National Historical Reserve. Both offer accessible hiking and camping options, educational opportunities, and beautiful natural settings.

---

## 1. Mount Rainier National Park

**Overview:**  
Mount Rainier is an iconic, glaciated volcano with subalpine meadows, ancient forests, and abundant wildlife. It offers accessible trails, educational ranger programs, and group-friendly campgrounds.

### Accessibility Highlights
- Cougar Rock Campground: 4 wheelchair-accessible sites, accessible restrooms, paved roads, and accessible amphitheater.
- White River Campground: Accessible restrooms in Loop C, paved roads, and hard-packed dirt campsites.
- Paradise Area: Henry M. Jackson Visitor Center is accessible, with accessible restrooms and exhibits.
- Many paved or hard-packed trails near Paradise and Longmire are suitable for wheelchairs and mobility devices.

### Campgrounds
- **Cougar Rock Campground** (Recommended for groups)
  - 179 sites, 133 reservable, 5 group sites (tent only), 4 accessible sites.
  - Amenities: flush toilets, potable water, amphitheater, food storage, camp store.
  - Reservations: [Recreation.gov - Cougar Rock](https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232466)
  - Fee: $20/night (group sites $60/night)
- **White River Campground**
  - 88 sites, all first-come, first-served, accessible restrooms.
  - Fee: $20/night

### Visitor Centers
- **Henry M. Jackson Memorial Visitor Center (Paradise)**
  - Open daily, 10:00 AM–4:30 PM. Accessible exhibits, restrooms, food, and gift shop.
- **Longmire Museum**
  - Open daily, 9:00 AM–4:30 PM. Accessible, with exhibits and ranger assistance.
- **Sunrise Visitor Center**
  - Open daily in summer, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM. Accessible exhibits and restrooms.

### Educational & Ranger-Led Events (July 3–7, 2025)
- **Paradise Plaza Ranger Program:** Daily, outside the Jackson Visitor Center. Stories, activities, and discussions about the park’s natural and cultural history.
- **Evening Program at Cougar Rock Campground Amphitheater:** July 12 (closest to your dates), ranger-led discussions on Mount Rainier’s human and natural history.
- **Evening Program at Paradise Inn Lobby:** July 11, ranger-led discussions.

### Current Alerts (2025)
- Ohanapecosh Campground and Visitor Center CLOSED for construction.
- Fire ban in effect: No campfires or charcoal grills.
- SR165 Carbon River/Fairfax Bridge closed: No access to Carbon River or Mowich Lake.
- Expect travel delays due to road work and long lines at entrances on weekends.
- Timed entry reservation required for Sunrise Corridor starting July 11 (not needed for your dates).

### Sample Itinerary (July 3–7)
- **Day 1:** Arrive at Cougar Rock Campground, set up camp, orientation, and accessible nature walk.
- **Day 2:** Visit Paradise area, accessible trails (e.g., Nisqually Vista Trail), attend Paradise Plaza Ranger Program.
- **Day 3:** Educational hike near Longmire, visit Longmire Museum, group picnic.
- **Day 4:** Explore accessible trails, attend evening ranger program at Cougar Rock Amphitheater.
- **Day 5:** Pack up, optional short hike or visitor center stop before departure.

---

## 2. Ebey’s Landing National Historical Reserve

**Overview:**  
Located on Whidbey Island, Ebey’s Landing preserves historic farmland, prairies, and coastal bluffs. It offers accessible hiking, group camping, and rich cultural history.

### Accessibility Highlights
- Bluff Trail: Hard-packed dirt, gentle grades, and spectacular views—suitable for many mobility devices.
- Jacob & Sarah Ebey House: Open Thurs–Sun, 10 AM–4 PM in summer.
- Visitor services and accessible restrooms available at state park facilities.

### Campgrounds
- **Fort Casey State Park** and **Fort Ebey State Park** (operated by Washington State Parks)
  - Both offer group and accessible campsites.
  - Reservations: [Washington State Parks Reservations](http://www.parks.wa.gov/)
  - Accessible restrooms and some accessible sites available.

### Visitor Centers
- No dedicated NPS visitor center, but interpretive signs and rangers are present at key sites.
- Administrative office open Mon–Fri, 9 AM–5
